items.title: Morrisons delivers strongest sales growth for a year as World Cup boosts business
items.summary: Morrisons delivered its strongest sales growth for a year as the World Cup helped to bring shoppers through its doors.
items.body:
Morrisons delivers strongest sales growth for a year as World Cup boosts business
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Morrisons delivered its strongest sales growth for a year as the World Cup helped to bring shoppers through its doors.
The struggling supermarket, which is in the process of a major turnaround, said hot weather and the football tournament lifted group like-for-like sales by 3.2 per cent over the 13 weeks to July 26.
Chief executive Rami Baitiéh, who took over as chief executive in November 2023, said it was 'clear evidence that our strategy is delivering and that we remain on track.'
Baitiéh has overseen price cuts to reverse Morrisons' fortunes after losing market share to German discounters Aldi and Lidl.
But he admitted that trading conditions ‘remained highly competitive’ amid a price war between major supermarkets that has seen similar price cutting schemes.
Morrisons says it is seeing progress in its turnaround, which has involved cutting prices
Even Waitrose, whose clientele are typically quite well-off, has been forced to cut prices to compete with competitors. The retailer today announced it was spending £20million on cutting the prices of just under 400 products by an average of 11 per cent.
Baitiéh added: ‘We traded strongly, growing ahead of the market and delivering a robust result, with an acceleration of like-for-like sales growth to 3.2 per cent. This is our strongest quarter since Q2 2025, and our fifteenth consecutive quarter of like-for-like growth.
He said keeping prices low was ‘key to this performance.’
Last month, Morrisons launched a new ‘unbeatable prices’ pledge across more than 500 everyday products. It promises that the products covered will cost the same or less than at Aldi, Asda, Lidl, Sainsbury’s and Tesco, which ‘has already had a positive impact.’
The retailer clung onto its market share of 8.4 per cent over the 12 weeks to 6 September, according to more recent figures from market researchers at Worldpanel by Numerator. And sales rose 2.8 per cent to £3.06billion.
The business has been struggling since it was taken over by private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) in 2021 and last year its debt pile hit £7.5billion.
Jonathan de Mello, founder and CEO at retail consultancy JDM Retail, said the results were still disappointing and ‘primarily the result of temporary cyclical boosts’.
He added: ‘Morrisons’ continues to underwhelm, despite the positive spin in their latest update.
‘Morrisons' perennial problem has always been its lack of a distinctive offer and a weaker convenience footprint relative to major rivals.
‘More importantly, the business remains hamstrung by the weight of its £7.5bn private equity debt. This financial stranglehold forces short-term, defensive cost-cutting and aggressive asset disposals just to manage leverage and service immense finance costs, rather than allowing Morrisons to invest for growth.’
It came as rival Asda – which has had similar difficulties in the wake of being taken over by private equity – yesterday said it was ‘in the foothills of recovery’. Worldpanel figures showed that sales increased 0.1 per cent to £4.17billion in the 12 weeks to September 6 – the first time they have grown since March 2024.

items.title: Tomra unveils space-saving reverse vending machine for convenience retailers
items.summary: Experienced reverse vending machine (RVM) manufacturer Tomra has unveiled a new small-format machine tailor made for convenience stores. It has introduced the “small-footprint, big performance” TOMRA B3 in the UK as retailers prepare for the introduction of a deposit return scheme (DRS) in 2027. From… This story continues at Tomra unveils space-saving reverse vending machine for convenience retailers Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
It has introduced the “small-footprint, big performance” TOMRA B3 in the UK as retailers prepare for the introduction of a deposit return scheme (DRS) in 2027.
From October next year, consumers will pay a refundable 20p deposit on eligible plastic drinks bottles and cans, which they’ll get back from retailers when they return their empty containers.
Tomra manufactures reverse vending machines (RVMs) that automate the return process and said it has designed TOMRA B3 with convenience stores and independent retailers in mind.
It occupies just 0.45sqm of floor space, enabling convenience retailers to benefit from offering automated returns, as well as accessing the higher handling fees available through automated collection.
“TOMRA B3 is the smallest reverse vending machine in our product portfolio, and gives convenience stores and independent retailers a practical way to automate returns without sacrificing valuable store space. It also provides customers with an easy and reliable return experience,” explained Sondre Henningsgård, managing director for Tomra Collection UK.
“At Tomra we want to enable retailers to invest in the right technology from day one and TOMRA B3 meets that need by offering proven technology in a smaller format, designed by an experienced partner that has over 95,000 machines operating all over the world.”
The machine can handle two types of containers – PET plastic and metal cans – and is also available on wheels, offering greater flexibility on where it can be positioned in the store.
Using barcode recognition, weight detection and image-based recognition, the company said TOMRA B3 accurately identifies containers to deliver a quick and seamless recycling experience.
Exchange for Change, the deposit return scheme operator, will pay retailers a handling fee for every drinks container they collect. Retailers who use automated collection will receive a higher handling fee.
“Convenience retailers are assessing the advantages of automating collection instead of handling containers manually, and the larger handling fee is just one of many incentives,” added Henningsgård.
“Having a reverse vending machine can save staff time and make the process easier for customers. We see in other DRS markets that shoppers value a quick and reliable return experience, and retailers that provide this can benefit from attracting shoppers.”
“We know that investing in a reverse vending machine is a significant decision for a convenience retailer. TOMRA B3 has been designed as a cost-effective and reliable answer for stores with limited space. Qualifying sites can also apply for grant funding through Exchange for Change, so we’d recommend retailers to check if they are eligible.”

items.title: Scotland store bosses reveal crime concerns as vaping display consultation continues
items.summary: Convenience store bosses in Scotland fear that forcing vaping products behind shutters could further fuel illicit trade. A consultation into how products are packaged and displayed as part of the Tobacco and Vapes Act runs until October 2 - with retailers being urged to make… This story continues at Scotland store bosses reveal crime concerns as vaping display consultation continues Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
A consultation into how products are packaged and displayed as part of the Tobacco and Vapes Act runs until October 2 – with retailers being urged to make their voices heard as part of it.
It seeks views on proposals which could lead to new rules around packaging and flavours, along with where and how products are displayed.
But prominent members of the Scottish Grocers’ Federation (SGF) are increasingly concerned that a retail display ban – equal to tobacco – could have the unintended consequence of increasing black market trade.
And, speaking as they consider consultation responses, they believe that could be more dangerous for everyone.
Spar operator Ryan Hutchison’s family have run a convenience store in Scone, Perthshire, for almost 70 years.
Speaking about the impact of a display ban and taking the products out of sight, he said: “I think it will push people underground.
“There’s a real risk that they will get vapes which might not be regulated or the right product – as well as the risk that those illicit traders sell to children.
“Placing the products behind shutters can also cause frustrations at the till with customers explaining what they would like to buy.”
Saleem Sadiq, who has run his Spar store in Renfrew for more than 30 years, added: “Illicit trade is already a big problem. Illegal sellers have no scruples.
“A display ban is only going to accelerate the situation we already face.”
SGF said it is supportive of moves to reduce vaping amongst young people, but is working to ensure that any potential retail display ban does not have unintended consequences for illicit trade, retail crime or the ability for adult cigarette smokers, who wish to quit, to switch to vaping.
It has already met with the Scottish government to discuss its widespread concerns around the issue of illicit trade as it impacts the convenience store sector.
Pete Cheema, SGF’s chief executive, said: “There is no question that vaping products should not be marketed or sold to children. But government must also recognise the vital role that responsible retailers – including our members – play in preventing under-age sales and delivering effective age-verification measures.
“Regulation must be proportionate, practical, and workable. Proposals to place vaping products behind shutters could make legal products less convenient to buy without reducing underlying demand. Instead, they risk creating opportunities for illicit traders and diverting sales from responsible retailers who operate within the law.
“While the Scottish government has acknowledged the problem of bogus vape sellers, it has failed to recognise that placing legal products behind shutters could drive more consumers towards the illicit market.
“Legislation must not create unintended consequences that benefit criminals and undermine responsible retailers. We believe that a retail display ban is a step too far.”
The continuing consultation covers a range of new restrictions on tobacco and vaping products and is being hosted by the UK government, but the proposals have been developed with the devolved governments in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
SGF said it is also concerned about the tight timetable for changes to be made, adding unnecessary pressure on struggling retailers.
The retail body, which will be submitting its own response, has been working on “sensible restrictions” with policymakers in recent years, as part of its Healthier Choices, Healthier Communities campaign.

items.body:
UK shoppers can benefit from Waitrose quality and values at even lower prices from today (Wednesday 16 September).
The grocer is lowering prices by an average of 11% across hundreds of fresh food, store cupboard staples, and household products.
Crucially, every price drop maintains Waitrose’s industry-leading standards for responsible sourcing and higher animal welfare. Waitrose is the only retailer with 100% free-range eggs, milk, cream and fresh pork, 100% British beef and lamb, and responsibly sourced fish across its own ranges.
Waitrose is also the only UK retailer where all its own brand chicken – fresh, frozen, processed and ingredient – meets Better Chicken Commitment standards or higher. This means we source all our chicken from British farms that raise a slower-growing breed, with more space to peck, roost and roam.
The savings cover everyday items customers buy regularly for breakfast, lunchboxes, and family meals, with reductions of 20% or more on products including porridge oats, bread, and orange juice, alongside potatoes, rice, apples, and tomatoes. More than half (56%) of the reduced products come from the value-focused Essential Waitrose range.
The latest investment takes Waitrose’s total investment in its New Lower Prices programme to more than £180m, with prices reduced across more than 1,000 products since the programme began in 2023.
And there is evidence that customers are responding. The previous round of New Lower Prices (May 2026) delivered a 4% year-on-year increase in sales across the 160 reduced lines, while Waitrose achieved its highest-ever Net Promoter Score for value for money1.
The latest price cuts also reflect changing customer priorities around eating well. Waitrose.com search data shows searches for ‘high protein’ foods have increased by 112% year-on-year2, while searches for ‘high fibre’ foods have increased by 51%3.
In response, 70% of the new reduced food lines meet official ‘healthier choice’ standards4, including more than 100 fibre-rich products and more than 60 high-protein options.
Nathan Ansell, Waitrose Chief Customer Officer, said: “September is a reset moment for households across the country. As families get back to their regular routines, we know customers are looking for ways to make their weekly shop work harder for their budgets.
“That’s why we’re investing £20m to lower the price of more than 370 everyday products, from breakfast and lunchbox staples to the ingredients people rely on for family meals.
“For Waitrose, great value has always meant more than simply a low price. It means exceptional quality, responsible sourcing and market-leading animal welfare too. We’re making everyday food more affordable while maintaining the standards our customers expect from us.”
The price cuts are available in Waitrose shops and online from Wednesday 16 September.

Up to 20 £10,000 grants will be available to young entrepreneurs aged 18–30 building businesses on eBay, as well as established eBay […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
eBay UK is launching its second Up & Running Grants programme in the UK, with this year’s edition focused on supporting the next generation of entrepreneurs and creating new opportunities for young people.
Up to 20 £10,000 grants will be available to young entrepreneurs aged 18–30 building businesses on eBay, as well as established eBay sellers looking to create jobs, apprenticeships or placements for young talent.
The programme launches as the latest ONS figures show 981,000 people aged 16–24 in the UK are not currently in education, employment or training – equivalent to 13% of the age group.
The Up & Running Grants: Young Entrepreneur Edition is open to:
- Young entrepreneurs aged 18 to 30 who are building a business on eBay
- eBay business sellers of any age looking to invest in the next generation of talent through employment, apprenticeships or placements
Successful applicants will receive support including:
- A £10,000 cash grant
- Up to six months of dedicated account management and premium customer service
- Access to eBay’s new Young Entrepreneur community and selected events throughout 2027
Eve Williams, General Manager of eBay UK, said: “The UK has no shortage of entrepreneurial ambition, and I’m constantly inspired by the young entrepreneurs I see building businesses on eBay across everything from sneakers and watches to electronics and trading cards. But turning an idea or side hustle into a thriving business takes the right backing.
“This year’s eBay Up & Running Grants are about giving young British entrepreneurs the funding, tools and support they need to take the next step, while helping established businesses create opportunities for the next generation.”
Nick Penglelly and Sue Black, owners of JustSeed, a previous Up & Running Grant winner, said: “The Up & Running grant has helped us further future-proof our business while creating an opportunity for a young person. By using the funding to invest in new digital tools and bring a new apprentice into our team, we’ve enhanced our customer service and made efficiencies across the business. It’s been a game changer for us, and we’re delighted to see how our newest recruit has been able to bloom.”
Applications open on 16 September 2026 and close at 5pm on 30 October 2026, with up to 20 successful businesses announced in January 2027.

items.title: Independent owner-operators remain dominant buyers of convenience stores
items.summary: Buyer demand continues to outstrip supply across UK convenience store and forecourt markets, Christie & Co reports. The specialist business property adviser has launched its Retail Market Review 2026, which provides insight into transaction activity, buyer demand, the trading environment, regulatory change and emerging opportunities… This story continues at Independent owner-operators remain dominant buyers of convenience stores Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The specialist business property adviser has launched its Retail Market Review 2026, which provides insight into transaction activity, buyer demand, the trading environment, regulatory change and emerging opportunities across the UK’s convenience store and forecourt sectors.
The report highlights a market underpinned by strong fundamentals, with both convenience stores and forecourts continuing to demonstrate adaptability despite high operating costs, labour challenges and regulatory change.
Christie & Co recorded a 26% increase in offers on retail businesses in H1 2026 compared with H1 2025, reflecting exceptionally strong buyer demand across both sectors.
Whilst it faces challenges common to all retail, the convenience store market remains one of the most active retail subsectors in the UK, supported by needs-based consumer spending, the continued growth of top-up shopping missions, and the vital role local stores play within their communities.
In the first half of 2026, Christie & Co sold more than 100 retail businesses, averaging four completed transactions every week, and in the convenience store market, independent owner-operators remained the dominant buyer group, accounting for 65% of acquisitions completed by Christie & Co.
In the forecourt market, demand continues to be driven by resilient fuel volumes, strong convenience retail performance and the evolution of sites into broader roadside retail destinations offering food-to-go, parcel services and electric vehicle charging facilities.
Demand remained strongest for high-quality freehold forecourt assets and established roadside retail destinations combining fuel, convenience retail and foodservice.
Freehold assets accounted for 73% of forecourt transactions completed by Christie & Co in H1 2026 reflecting the continued interest in the underlying property.
While market confidence remains relatively high, retailers continue to face significant challenges including labour costs, staffing shortages and rising compliance requirements.
The report examines several regulatory developments set to impact operators, including the Tobacco and Vapes Act, the Deposit Return Scheme, and restrictions on energy drink sales to under-16s, presenting both challenges and opportunities for operators over the months ahead.
At the same time, businesses are increasingly embracing technology and AI-powered solutions to improve operational efficiency, manage costs and enhance the customer experience.
Crime and security remain major concerns across the sector, with retailers investing heavily in measures such as CCTV, body-worn cameras, ANPR technology and enhanced loss-prevention systems to protect staff, property, and profits.
The increased time and resources required to manage add further management costs for businesses, creating additional inflationary pressures at a time when the government is seeking to bring inflation under control.
The review outlines that well-invested businesses with a strong local presence, diversified income streams, and clear growth strategies are best placed to succeed, and continue to attract significant buyer interest.
For convenience stores, growth is expected to be driven by food-to-go, home delivery, parcel services and community-led retailing along with cost control measures.
Investment in forecourts including EV charging where appropriate, and an enhanced convenience offer is expected to remain a key driver of value creation.
Steve Rodell, managing director – retail & leisure at Christie & Co, said, “The confidence we are seeing from purchasers reflects the essential role that both convenience stores and forecourts play within communities and infrastructure across the country.
“These businesses continue to benefit from strong local customer loyalty, and increasingly diverse revenue streams that extend beyond traditional retail and fuel sales.
“Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the outlook for both subsectors. Whilst challenges undoubtedly remain, particularly with several major new initiatives and regulations set to impact operators in the coming months, the market fundamentals underpinning convenience retail and forecourts are as strong as ever.”

items.body:
Women’s cricket in the United States is taking a major step forward as the inaugural Seattle Orcas Women’s T20 Exhibition launched in August, creating new competitive opportunities for female players and helping accelerate the growth of the game across the country.
British female-founded cricket brand Maiden Cricket, recently seen on Dragons’ Den, has been named the tournament’s founding apparel 
The partnership comes after a landmark summer for the women’s game in the UK, with record-breaking crowds, growing participation and increased investment continuing to raise the profile of female cricket. With cricket returning to the Olympic Games at Los An
Although an estimated 500 women play cricket across the US, only around 20 are regularly in contention for the national team, with many players averaging just 35 competitive matches over seven or eight years. The inaugural Seattle Orcas Women’s T20 Exhibition has been created to help address that gap, bringing together leading international players alongside some of America’s top domestic talent in a high-performance environment designed to strengthen the pathway towards a future Major League Cricket Women (MLC-W).
Founded by teenage sisters Honor and Cat Black after growing frustrated with playing in kit designed for boys, Maiden was created to ensure female cricketers had equipment built specifically for them.
The partnership sees Maiden supply match kit, training wear and specialist equipment, including women’s batting pads, wicketkeeping pads and gloves, ensuring every player has access to products designed specifically for female athletes.
Leading Maiden Cricket US is 16-year-old Aashna Jain, Owner of Maiden Cricket US A longtime follower of cricket, Aashna saw an opportunity to introduce Maiden’s female-first approach to a US market where interest and opportunities in the sport continue to expand.
“I’ve followed cricket for years, and I’m excited to bring Maiden to the US,” said Aashna Jain. “I want girls to have access to cricket apparel and equipment designed specifically for female players and to feel like there is a place for them in the sport. I hope Maiden can inspire more girls to get involved in the game.”
Honor Black, Co-Founder of Maiden Cricket, said:
“When Cat and I started Maiden, it came from our own experience of loving cricket but never feeling like the game had been designed with girls in mind. We wanted to change that.
“We’ve seen women’s cricket grow so much over the past few years, especially here in the UK, and it’s really exciting to see that momentum building in the US too.
“We’re incredibly proud to support the inaugural Seattle Orcas Women’s T20 Exhibition. We hope it inspires more women and girls across the US to pick up a bat and see cricket as a sport where they belong.”
Sean Cary, CEO of the Seattle Orcas, said:
“This exhibition is an important opportunity to showcase the talent that already exists in women’s cricket and create a competitive environment where players can continue to develop.”
“We wanted a kit partner that understood the specific needs of female cricketers, and Maiden brings that perspective to the tournament. We’re excited to be working together and help establish an event that can continue to grow in the years ahead.”
Anika Kolan, USA Women’s senior team player and Maiden Cricket US athlete ambassador, said: “Being part of the first US women’s cricket tournament is an important milestone for the sport and for the players who have been working to grow the game here.”
“Women cricketers need opportunities to compete at a high level and show the talent that already exists in the US and North America. Having uniforms and equipment designed specifically for female players makes this moment even more meaningful. It shows that women’s cricket is being taken seriously, and I’m proud to be part of it.”
The tournament features three teams competing in six round-robin matches before a final, with fixtures streamed nationally alongside youth activities and family-focused events designed to help inspire the next generation of players and fans.

items.title: Lidl makes UK retail first on living income for Kenyan tea farmers
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Tea – the first in the UK designed to directly support closing the living income gap for Kenyan tea growers. Through Lidl GB’s Fairtrade tea, farmers in Kenya earn the Fairtrade Minimum Price for tea, and The Fairtrade […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Marking Fairtrade Fortnight, Lidl GB is launching a British retailer-first product with its new Way To Go! Tea – the first in the UK designed to directly support closing the living income gap for Kenyan tea growers.
Through Lidl GB’s Fairtrade tea, farmers in Kenya earn the Fairtrade Minimum Price for tea, and The Fairtrade Premium, an extra sum of money for farmers to invest in their farms and communities. On top of that, the Way to Go! Tea is the first of its kind, working closely with Fairtrade, to calculate a Living Income Reference Price for tea farmers and is paying an additional amount per kg of tea to go towards supporting farmer livelihoods.
In Britain, around 100 million cups of tea are drunk every single day. While standard certifications provide vital protections for tea-growing communities, achieving a true living income remains an industry-wide hurdle. This new launch is designed to build on Lidl GB’s existing 100% certified own-brand tea commitment, exploring how targeted premiums can directly support closing the living income gap for smallholders.
This launch is the latest step in Lidl GB’s long-term ethical sourcing strategy. Lidl GB were the first retailer to conduct a Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) focused on Kenyan tea. As part of the action plan resulting from this, the discounter pledged to support systemic change in the tea sector by working towards living wages and incomes.
Holly Bleach, senior buying director at Lidl GB, said: “Through this new product we’re aiming to make a real difference to the everyday lives of Kenyan farmers. Every brew represents the hard work of a farmer and their family, and, as a responsible business, we believe that work must be rewarded fairly. By paying a living income premium directly to growers, we are helping these farmers secure the stable future they’ve earned.”
Kerrina Thorogood, Partnerships Director at the Fairtrade Foundation, said: “We’re delighted that Lidl will be going beyond the Fairtrade Minimum Price and Fairtrade Premium with its new Way To Go! tea, committing to pay smallholder tea farmers in Kericho, Kenya, an additional amount on every kilogram of tea it buys, tailored to reflect local living income needs. This commitment to helping close the living income gap is a significant and very welcome step towards fair pay for tea growers.
Fair pay is fundamental to the future of the tea sector. Today, just one in five tea farmers in Kenya earns enough income each month to support their families with the essentials. As a result, many struggle to invest in their farms, adapt to climate change, and plan for the future. Addressing this challenge requires businesses to take responsibility for the prices they pay.
We welcome Lidl’s commitment – and this new approach to living income in tea – as an important addition to the substantial efforts already underway by Fairtrade partners across the tea sector. We hope it will encourage others to follow suit. Meaningful change for the people who grow our tea still requires more businesses to step up and increase their sourcing of Fairtrade tea. We need action at sector level scale to move towards fairer pay and close the living income gap for tea farmers and workers.”
For over 16 years, Lidl has partnered with Fairtrade, a commitment that spans over 100 certified products throughout the year. Last year alone through Lidl Fairtrade sales, producers earned over £1.9million in Fairtrade Premium, an extra sum of money invested in areas such as farming improvements and community initiatives of their choice.
Across Lidl GB’s tea range, the discounter has reached a major milestone in its strategic partnership with WWF by achieving its ambitious tea certification target. Today, 100% of the raw material across Lidl GB’s own-brand tea range – including all private-label black, green, and rooibos teas – is certified by Rainforest Alliance or Fairtrade standards. This achievement reinforces the discounter’s long-standing commitment to human rights and responsible sourcing, following the successful fulfilment of all its 2025 raw material goals.
Lidl GB’s new Way To Go! Single Origin Kenyan Tea lands in stores nationwide at the end of September, priced at £1.99 for 80 bags. The tea bags will be made from 100% plant based fibres and so are biodegradable and suitable for composting.

items.body:
Arrowtown (www.arrowtowndrinks.co.uk), one of the UK’s fastest-growing ready-to-drink (RTD) brands, has secured a major nationwide listing with Morrisons. Launching in September, the brand’s premium, all-natural Vodka Sodas will hit the shelves of all Morrisons stores in time for entertaining season. Having secured a national Sainsbury’s listing in July this year, Arrowtown’s availability is wider than ever; wholesalers include LWC, Molson Coors, Imbibe Melrose, Matthew Clark, Dayla, Stores Supply, Craft Drink Co, CLF, Organica Food & Wine and Champers.
Morrisons will stock two of Arrowtown’s signature (there are four delicious products in the range), full-flavour variants: Mango & Pineapple and Black Cherry & Apple. Both come in 330ml cans at 4.5% ABV, with an RRP of £2.95.
Matt Brittain, Buyer at Morrisons, comments, “The branding looks awesome, but more importantly, the drink itself actually tastes good. It’s hard to find a truly clean, better-for-you option that doesn’t sacrifice flavour, so it’s a total win for anyone trying to drink a bit smarter.”
Market data reveals that 57% of adults are actively taking steps to cut their sugar intake, while 45% of consumers globally now judge the overall health of a product strictly by its sugar levels. As shoppers reject sugary alcopops, the premium sector of the RTD market is exploding, witnessing a massive 84% year-on-year growth.
Arrowtown sits squarely at the intersection of two massive consumer trends: the booming growth of the RTD market and the ever-growing shift toward health-conscious drinking. Proudly made in the UK, the range is crafted with triple-distilled vodka, sparkling soda, and 100% natural ingredients. Boasting premium flavours, low sugar, and just 109 kcal per can, Arrowtown avoids the artificial sweeteners common in competitors to deliver a delicious, lighter alternative to traditional alcoholic beverages.
Two Brothers thirsty for change
The inspiration for Arrowtown was born in 2021 when brothers James and Rob Smith were traveling through New Zealand straight out of university. While exploring the Otago region of New Zealand’s South Island, they discovered a local appreciation for lighter vodka-and-soda pairings, a massive trend they also saw exploding via hard seltzers in the US.
Inspired by Arrowtown, a picturesque and historic gold-mining village they visited, the brothers returned to the UK determined to do things differently. Armed with their degrees and a desire to take on the world’s biggest drinks brands, James (then 22) and Rob (then 24) launched Arrowtown to create a drink fit for the 21st-century consumer.
“The world of alcohol consumption is changing,” says co-Founder James Smith. “Consumers want transparency, sustainable authenticity, and great taste without the artificial ingredients. We wanted to make a drink that keeps the good times flowing but aligns with a modern, balanced lifestyle.”
630,000 Bottles Saved From our Oceans
Born and raised in a coastal town, the Smith brothers are driven by an environmental mission to protect the natural world, Arrowtown has baked sustainability directly into its core operations. Through an official partnership with Ocean Co., every single can of Arrowtown enjoyed funds the collection and removal of two ocean-bound plastic bottles, stopping them from ever reaching our oceans. 630,000 bottles saved and counting.
With its nationwide rollout this September, Arrowtown is primed to bring its refreshing drinks to a massive new audience.

The multi-year partnership will see THG Commerce design, build and power The Entertainer’s next-generation digital […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
The Entertainer, the UK’s leading independent toy retailer, has appointed THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, as its new digital commerce partner, accelerating its transformation and opening up new ways for customers to discover and shop for toys online and in-store.
The multi-year partnership will see THG Commerce design, build and power The Entertainer’s next-generation digital experience, creating a more intuitive, inspiring and personalised journey for families, gift buyers and the growing number of adult toy and collectible enthusiasts.
The investment is a further step in The Entertainer’s journey to build a world-class omnichannel customer experience, combining the expertise, curation and sense of discovery customers value in its stores with the convenience and personalisation of modern digital retail.
Toy shopping is a uniquely varied and discovery-led experience. Customers may be buying for their own children, choosing gifts for family or friends, shopping for birthdays or seasonal occasions, or increasingly buying toys and collectibles for themselves. They may know the relevant age, interest, occasion or budget they are aiming for without having a clear idea of the specific product they are looking for.
The new experience will be designed around those different customer missions. THG Commerce will deploy AI-enabled shopping assistance, conversational discovery and intent-led search capabilities to help customers explore thousands of products and find the right choice more intuitively.
These capabilities draw on the wider THG Ingenuity collaboration with Google Cloud, which harnesses Vertex AI Commerce Search and Gemini to develop next-generation AI-powered commerce services. THG Commerce’s AI solutions are built on its modular architecture, enabling individual capabilities to operate independently of the underlying storefront, be deployed as standalone, platform-agnostic services.
Alongside smarter search and discovery, the new experience will bring together richer content, curated product journeys and personalised recommendations to inspire customers throughout the purchasing journey. THG Commerce will deliver a new web and mobile experience, together with an enhanced Click & Collect journey designed to create a more seamless connection between digital discovery and The Entertainer’s nationwide store network.
The new platform is expected to launch in Spring 2027 and has been designed to provide a foundation for future innovation, including future opportunities across loyalty, retail media and social commerce as The Entertainer continues to develop its omnichannel customer proposition.
Malcolm Carter, digital & marketing Director, The Entertainer, said: “Our ambition is to redefine the experience for anyone looking to discover and buy toys, whether they are shopping for their children, choosing a gift for someone else or buying for themselves. Toy shopping should be joyful and inspiring, but the sheet breadth of choice means customers increasingly need help navigating it. We have a real opportunity to combine the expertise, trusted brands and passion for play people associate with The Entertainer with intelligent technology that helps customers find something they’ll love. Partnering with THG Commerce gives us the technology, capability and ambition to reimagine that experience across digital, stores and wherever our customers choose to shop in an increasing AI-centric landscape. This is an important investment in the next generation of The Entertainer and in how we serve our customers.”
Darren Rajanah, chief revenue officer, THG Ingenuity, said: “The Entertainer is one of the most recognisable names in UK toy retail. Toy retail is a particularly rich discovery environment. Customers arrive with very different missions, from gifting and family purchases to collecting, and technology can play a powerful role in helping them navigate choice and discover the right products. The Entertainer get AI-enabled shopping assistance and CRM-integrated enhanced personalisation at launch, then a roadmap into loyalty, retail media and social commerce, backed by our wider THG Studios capabilities which can bring a new range to life on site quickly. We have built our AI capabilities to work anywhere, as standalone services that integrate with any commerce platform, so brands can benefit from them whether or not they replatform with us. We look forward to working closely with The Entertainer team to support their long-term growth ambitions.”

items.title: Baby, kids and toys emerges as UK’s strongest retail category as grocery falls behind, EY research finds

Consumer perceptions of UK retailers have improved over the past 12 months, but rising expectations are creating a widening gap between winners and losers, according to EY’s latest Retail Performance Index. The UK’s Baby, Kids and Toys sector emerged as the highest-rated retail category among consumers, while Grocery has fallen to the bottom of the rankings, […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Consumer perceptions of UK retailers have improved over the past 12 months, but rising expectations are creating a widening gap between winners and losers, according to EY’s latest Retail Performance Index.
The UK’s Baby, Kids and Toys sector emerged as the highest-rated retail category among consumers, while Grocery has fallen to the bottom of the rankings, according to the report.
The study, based on feedback from more than 10,000 UK consumers across over 200 retailers, found customer sentiment has improved across almost every retail category since 2023. However, growing consumer expectations are making it increasingly difficult for retailers to maintain a competitive edge.
The Baby, Kids and Toys category climbed two places in 2026 to take the top spot in rankings, overtaking all other retail categories. Health, Beauty and Wellness ranked second, while Sports and Outdoors continued to gain ground with both sectors benefiting from long-term shifts in consumer behaviour towards physical health, mental wellbeing and active lifestyles.
At the other end of the rankings, Grocery dropped three places to rank last, making it the only category to record a decline in consumer perception since 2023.

| Rank | Category | Median score 2026 | Rank change from 2023 | Median change from 2023 | 
| 1 | Baby, Kids & Toys | 64.4 | +2 | + 1.8 | 
| 2 | Health, Beauty & Wellness | 64.2 | – | + 1.2 | 
| 3 | Accessories | 62.9 | -2 | -2.1 | 
| 4 | Sports & Outdoors | 62.5 | – | + 2.0 | 
| 5 | Electronics | 61.0 | – | + 0.8 | 
| 6 | Footwear | 60.9 | – | + 0.7 | 
| 7 | Home & Garden | 59.9 | – | + 1.3 | 
| 8 | Convenience Food Service | 58.7 | +1 | + 0.5 | 
| 9 | Clothing | 58.5 | +2 | + 1.1 | 
| 10 | Books, Crafts & Stationers | 57.9 | – | + 0.3 | 
| 11 | Grocery | 57.8 | -3 | – 0.4 | 
Silvia Rindone, EY-Parthenon UK&I retail lead, said: “Our latest findings suggest that emotionally driven spending categories are proving the most resilient as households continue to manage economic pressures.
“The retailers that are winning consumer favour today are often the ones positioned to win market share tomorrow. What makes this year’s findings particularly interesting is that the best-performing categories are those that have tapped into powerful emotional and lifestyle drivers.
“Consumers continue to prioritise spending on children, health and wellbeing, even when household budgets remain under pressure creating opportunities that genuinely understand evolving customer needs.”
Grocery falls behind as customer expectations rise
The research highlights growing divergence with grocery retail, with the gap between the strongest and weakest performers widening. Continued inflationary pressures and the frequency with which consumers interact with grocery retailers have made shoppers increasingly sensitive to value and service standards.
Silvia Rindone, added: “Grocery retailers are facing a unique challenge because customers interact with them more frequently than almost any other retail category. That means every price increase, stock availability issue or service failure is far more visible.
“The result is a category where leaders are pulling away from the pack, creating a much clearer distinction between those delivering consistently strong experiences and those struggling to keep pace.”
Middle market under pressure
Despite improving sentiment across retail sector, the EY Retail Performance Index found many retailers are increasingly being squeezed in the middle.
The study shows that both top-performing and lower-performing retailers have improved their customer perception scores since 2023, while median performers have seen far less progress.
Capabilities that once differentiated retailers, including seamless digital experiences and integrated online and in-store journeys, are now considered the norm by consumers.
“What was previously viewed as innovative just a few years ago is increasingly now regarded as standard practice,” said Silvia Rindone.
“Retailers cannot rely on simply keeping pace with competitors. The businesses creating sustainable advantage are the ones identifying what matters most to customers and investing in the areas that genuinely influence perception and loyalty.”

Exclusive opening day celebrations include Chief Design & Product Officer Zoe Price-Smith officially reopening the store, complimentary embroidery, expert bra fittings, goody bags and more
Boux Avenue, the accessible luxury lingerie, swimwear and nightwear retailer, is inviting customers to celebrate the reopening of its Belfast store in Victoria Square Shopping Centre on Friday 25th September from 11am. This follows a two week refurbishment to introduce the brand’s bright new retail concept to the store.
The Belfast store upgrade forms part of Boux Avenue’s continued investment in its physical retail estate, following a programme of new store openings and refurbishments throughout 2025 and 2026. The brand opened a new Manchester Arndale store in August 2025, before introducing its latest retail concept at a new site in Liverpool One in May 2025, a larger site in Manchester’s Trafford Centre for its Northern Flagship store in November 2025, followed by refitting its Southern Flagship store in Bluewater in March 2026
Clean and contemporary, across the newly refitted Belfast store, customers will discover a new frontage design with improved sight lines, contemporary signage and enhanced digital displays. Inside, new eco lighting complements softer interior finishes and updated merchandising fixtures, maximising space and product visibility. The concierge area, adjacent to Boux Avenue’s fitting suites with their personalised lighting options and call
buttons, has also been refreshed with a semi-circular seating area, allowing friends and family to relax while customers enjoy the brand’s complimentary expert bra fitting service.
Chief design & product officer Zoe Price-Smith will officially reopen the store on Friday 25th September at 11am with a ribbon-cutting ceremony, welcoming customers as they discover Boux Avenue’s refreshed Belfast store.
To celebrate the reopening, the first 50 customers who spend £50 or more will receive an exclusive Boux Avenue goody bag. Customers will also have the opportunity to personalise selected purchases at a complimentary embroidery station.
Throughout Friday 25th and Saturday 26th September, Boux Avenue’s team of expert bra fitting specialists will be available to help shoppers find their perfect fit. On Friday, customers can also enjoy live music from DJ and Q Radio presenter Amy McGuckin, alongside complimentary non-alcoholic refreshments for the first hour. Customers can also enjoy complimentary embroidery in store on Friday and Saturday, with the embroidery service available from 11am–5pm on Saturday, adding a personalised touch to their Boux Avenue purchases. Customers visiting on opening day will be among the first to shop Boux Avenue’s Autumn/Winter collection, including the sultry new Rococo Drama lingerie and nightwear collection alongside the luxurious Chocolate & Roses nightwear range.
Ahead of the official reopening, Boux Avenue will host an exclusive press and influencer evening at the newly refurbished Belfast store on Thursday 24th September from 6pm–8pm. Guests will be among the first to experience the new store, with Chief Design & Product Officer Zoe Price-Smith hosting a presentation and product preview, alongside drinks, a live DJ, complimentary embroidery, goody bags and Boux Avenue’s expert bra fitting service.
“We’re delighted to welcome our customers back to our newly refurbished Belfast store and celebrate this exciting milestone with the local community. Our new retail concept has been designed to create a brighter, more contemporary shopping environment, making it even easier for customers to discover our latest collections while enjoying the expert bra fitting service for which Boux Avenue is renowned.
“Victoria Square is a fantastic location for us, and we’re really looking forward to welcoming our Belfast customers back into the store and celebrating the reopening with them,” said Price-Smith.

items.body:
Wooden spoons are doubling as microphones in kitchens across Britain, as six in ten people (59%) say they love turning up the tunes for an impromptu kitchen disco, new research reveals.
And when the music starts, anything goes, with more than a quarter (26%) admitting they have grabbed a kitchen utensil, such as a wooden spoon, and used it as a makeshift microphone.
The survey of 2,000 UK adults1, commissioned by home improvement retailer Wickes, found that a third (33%) believe the kitchen is the best room in the house for a boogie, while more than eight in ten (88%) insist it really is the heart of the family home.
Saturday is the most popular day for a kitchen disco, according to half of those polled, with the typical party kicking off at around 3.30pm and lasting for 37 minutes – just enough time to work off lunch or build up an appetite for dinner.
For one in five, what began as a civilised party has even ended in guests abandoning their seats and taking over the kitchen dancefloor. And it’s the sounds of the eighties that are most likely to get families throwing shapes, with 43% favouring hits from the decade. This is followed by 37% opting for nineties pop classics, and 29% preferring to turn up the volume for a rock anthem.
Some of the nation’s favourite disco tracks have also been revealed, including the likes of Queen and Abba, while Come on Eileen by Dexys Midnight Runners also hits the list with 19%.
Just behind are Journey’s air-punching classic Don’t Stop Believin’ 
Dancefloor favourites Uptown Funk, It’s Raining Men, Simply the Best and Sex on Fire were each backed by 17%, while eighties favourites including a-ha’s Take on Me, Toto’s Africa, the Bee Gees’ Night Fever and Madonna’s Vogue also feature in the wider list.
They’re joined by crowd-pleasers from Fleetwood Mac, Van Morrison and Sister Sledge, alongside newer favourites from Rihanna, Beyoncé, Miley Cyrus, Harry Styles, Dua Lipa and Sabrina Carpenter, showing kitchen discos span the generations and proving that families do not only rely on golden oldies to get the party started.
To bring the findings to life, Wickes has partnered with Bauer Media to launch Kimberley Walsh’s Kitchen Rhythms with Wickes playlist – 15-tracks designed for cooking, cleaning and dancing at home – available on Magic Radio and available on Rayo.
Music is already helping Brits take the drudgery out of everyday kitchen jobs, with 58% saying it makes washing up easier.
Half (50%) put on tunes while cooking dinner, while 46% listen when mopping the floor and 38% do so while wiping down surfaces.
More than half (55%) say music is vital for motivating them to clean the kitchen, while 46% choose what to play depending on their mood.
When it comes to the family member with the best moves, mum takes the crown, with a third (32%) saying she can throw the best shapes. Dad comes second on 21%, narrowly beating the family teenager on 20%.
Nearly three in ten families (29%) even have a special family anthem – a go-to track guaranteed to get everyone singing, dancing or reminiscing together – while over two in five (41%) believe a shared family boogie brings the generations together and helps everyone feel closer.
The findings reflect the role kitchens play beyond cooking, with Wickes Design Consultants seeing customers increasingly looking for spaces that work just as well for spending time together and entertaining, as they do for everyday meals.
Kitchen islands and breakfast bars create social hubs within the home, while clever storage solutions and layered lighting help keep spaces practical and welcoming. The Wickes Design Consultants are experts in creating a space equally suited to family mealtimes, entertaining guests and those spontaneous moments that bring people together.
Paul Bangs, Category Director of Kitchens and Bathrooms at Wickes, added: “The kitchen really is the heart of the home, and our research shows it’s now also the dance floor for many families. A kitchen needs to work hard for everyday life, from cooking and cleaning to entertaining, and those spontaneous moments that bring everyone together. We have a range of kitchens at Wickes and a team of experts to help create a kitchen you love spending time in, whether that’s for cooking or having an impromptu dance.”

items.title: Lancashire Spar retailers sponsor new covers at local cricket club
items.summary: Two Lancashire Spar independent retailers are supporting their local cricket club by sponsoring new covers. Jonty Collinson and Mark Follen have paired up to cover the cost of the new ground equipment at Shireshead and Forton Cricket Club. The red covers are branded up with… This story continues at Lancashire Spar retailers sponsor new covers at local cricket club Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Jonty Collinson and Mark Follen have paired up to cover the cost of the new ground equipment at Shireshead and Forton Cricket Club.
The red covers are branded up with Spar and Cheeky Coffee logos with Jonty selling the coffee brand at his nearby Cabus and Scorton stores, and Mark at his Brock and Forton forecourt sites.
Shireshead and Forton Cricket Club has a long history dating back to 1909 and the club plays in both the Palace Shield and Westmorland Cricket League.
Cricket is also introduced to up to 40 children through the ECB’s All Stars Cricket programme and the ground is used for practice or matches daily throughout the regular season at an average of four games per week.
Collinson said: “The covers really standout and look fantastic on the ground. One of the downsides of the fantastic summer we have enjoyed, however, is that they have hardly been used so we have had to wait until September for the rain!
“Cricket covers are an expensive purchase, and you need to invest in quality to ensure the ground is properly protected from the elements when it rains. They stood up to the sharp showers we have had this last week or so, and they will be great for many seasons ahead.
“Mark and I are both long-standing supporters of the club, having been involved different ways for many years. We saw the covers as an opportunity to extend our support, and we are both delighted with the outcome.
“Somewhere in the region of 80 to 100 matches are played on the ground per season when you include hosting matches for league representative teams and Lancaster University teams.
“We have significant plans in place to develop the club house facilities and secure cricket for the next group of juniors and meet the demands of a growing population in Forton too.”

items.body:
Jigsaw has appointed Melanie Walker as Design Director to lead the next chapter of the brand’s product and creative direction.
Walker brings more than two decades of experience across luxury and contemporary fashion, with a track record of turning a clear creative point of view into collections that sell.
The appointment comes as Jigsaw’s turnaround continues to build momentum. The brand this week reported an 18% year-on-year increase in sales for Spring/Summer 2026, with growth across stores, online and concessions, building on a Christmas 2025 trading period in which sales rose 26%.
Product drove the season, with dresses up 43% on the strength of occasion wear and print. Walker’s brief is to build on that: more of the pieces customers are already buying, a sharper and more recognisable Jigsaw signature, and a product offer that holds its shape as the brand grows across channels and into the US.
Walker joined Victoria Beckham in 2008 as the brand’s first employee. She played a key role in establishing the brand’s ready-to-wear infrastructure and was promoted to Head of Design, Ready-to- Wear in 2013, leading the design and development of mainline and pre-collections and overseeing the design and studio teams.
Her career began at Roland Mouret, followed by Jonathan Saunders and FREDA, the in-house womenswear label at Matches Fashion, where she became Head of Design. Since 2017, she has worked as an independent design consultant to luxury and contemporary brands including Hurlingham 1875, Alice Made This and Paper London. Most recently, she led revitalization and rebrand of all uniform design for Abercrombie & Kent’s as part of their global brand repositioning.
Walker’s appointment follows Jigsaw’s strategic reset in 2025, which installed a refreshed leadership team led by Tikki Godley as Managing Director, and the appointment of Chris Browne as Retail Director in April 2026 to lead the opening of 10 new UK stores. The brand launches this Autumn/Winter through the Nordstrom and Macy’s marketplaces in the US.
Commenting on her appointment, Melanie Walker said: “It is a great honour to join Jigsaw as Design Director. I have always been inspired by the rich history of this British brand and its strong connection to arts and culture. Excellent quality, fit and fabric will be at the forefront of every design decision. I look forward to working with the Atelier team to craft the next chapter of this iconic brand’s story.”
Tikki Godley, Managing Director at Jigsaw, said: “I have followed Melanie’s career over the years and am confident she will bring a creative and modern vision to Jigsaw, inspired by our rich history making clothes for people who care about how clothes are made: quality, fit and fabric, and a commitment to backing British design. Melanie will be supported by our wonderful team in the Atelier who will bring her creativity to life.”

items.body:
Mike Ashley tightens grip on Hugo Boss as son-in-law made chair
Mike Ashley has tightened his grip on Hugo Boss after his son-in-law, the boss of Frasers Group, was made chairman of the German fashion house.
Frasers, which Ashley founded as Sports Direct, has been vying for control of Hugo Boss for months, resulting in him toppling the chairman of its supervisory board, Stefan Sturm, earlier this week.
The group said on Wednesday that Michael Murray, Ashley’s son-in-law, will succeed Sturm as chair of the panel, which oversees the fashion brand’s managing board and appoints its members.
“Together with my colleagues on the supervisory board and the managing board, I look forward to building on the company’s strong foundation and supporting the execution of its strategic priorities,” Murray said.
Frasers pushed up its holding in Hugo Boss to nearly 48 per cent after offering €38 per share to existing investors in the group, after the firm’s board slapped down its “inadequate” direct takeover offer.
Frasers shares dip
Ashley’s group, which is pushing into up-market fashion and away from Sports Direct’s discount roots, has told investors that it wants to push its holding in Hugo Boss above the 50 per cent mark.
Shares in Frasers, which trades on the FTSE 250, fell nearly five per cent on Wednesday morning, to 746.25p.
Sturm stepped down as supervisory board chair on Monday, saying that “recent changes in the company’s shareholder structure” meant it was an “appropriate point in time for an orderly transition” of power.
Murray has served as Frasers Group’s chief executive since 2022. He said on Wednesday that he wants to take advantage of Hugo Boss’s “untapped potential”.
He added: “By ensuring continuity and maintaining a clear long-term perspective, we will focus on unlocking the full potential of Hugo Boss and creating sustainable value for all shareholders and stakeholders.”
Ashley has said that the luxury brands which Frasers works with view Murray as a more likeable figurehead, describing his son-in-law as “the pretty boy”. He told the Financial Times last month: “I’m Marmite – I’m not everyone’s cup of tea.”
Daniel Greder, chief executive of the German fashion house, said he is confident that Murray and Frasers support the group’s existing strategy.
He added: “As the managing board, we look forward to further pursuing our course with discipline, focus, and clear commitment.
“We will work closely with Michael Murray and the Supervisory Board to realise our strategic and financial ambitions and create sustainable value.”
Sports Direct, which Ashley founded in 1982, surged to prominence for selling sportswear at rock-bottom prices. But last month, Frasers snapped up struggling department store chain Harvey Nichols to boost the visibility of its luxury label, Flannels.
Frasers has garnered a reputation for taking stakes in rival companies – like Boohoo and Mulberry – and using these positions to make aggressive plays for change within the firm.

items.title: Datacenter rush will create ‘tsunami’ of discarded electronics, report says
items.summary: Global push will triple toxic e-waste annually in 25 years, filling enough shipping containers to circle globe six times The ongoing campaign to build thousands of massive datacenters for AI will create a “tsunami” of discarded electronics, putting the world on a course to triple its annual generation of toxic e-waste in the next 25 years, a new report projects. The electronic trash AI generates in the next 25 years could fill enough shipping containers to encircle the globe six times, it said. Yet, says the report by the non-profit environmental group Basel Action Network (BAN), there is no plan to deal with that waste – which typically contains toxics like lead, mercury, cadmium and forever chemicals, as well as valuable metals that are challenging to reclaim. Continue reading...
items.body:
The ongoing campaign to build thousands of massive datacenters for AI will create a “tsunami” of discarded electronics, putting the world on a course to triple its annual generation of toxic e-waste in the next 25 years, a new report projects.
The electronic trash AI generates in the next 25 years could fill enough shipping containers to encircle the globe six times, it said. Yet, says the report by the non-profit environmental group Basel Action Network (BAN), there is no plan to deal with that waste – which typically contains toxics like lead, mercury, cadmium and forever chemicals, as well as valuable metals that are challenging to reclaim.
“Already electronic waste is the fastest-growing waste stream on the planet and only one-fifth is properly managed,” said Jim Puckett, co-founder of BAN, which works to see that toxic waste doesn’t end up getting dumped on the world’s poorer communities.
Experts concur. “We’re doing a terrible job of handling e-waste in the US,” said Vince Beiser, author of the book Power Metal, which details the global problems of trying to reclaim valuable metals inside electronic goods. “Some of it gets dumped overseas. Most of it just gets dumped in landfills, which is a problem because it can leach all kinds of nasty things into the water, into the soil.”
There are 4,871 new datacenters in the construction pipeline in the US, the report said, adding that, while not all are clearly designated for use by AI, many will be.
It calculated the volumes of e-waste related to computer servers used for AI, and to “the thousands of tonnes of copper, steel, concrete” for cooling, power distribution, networking and energy storage equipment needed to operate inside datacenters.
To estimate the total, the report estimated the amount of computing power analysts project will be built – totalling roughly 100 gigawatts of new capacity worldwide by 2030 alone and growing beyond that. It then analyzed how much equipment would be needed by weight – including racks of computer servers weighing 1,360kgs each, switches that weigh up to 30kgs, and hundreds of kilograms of copper cable connecting each rack.
Such equipment won’t be designed for repair and reuse, the report projects, and would need to be completely replaced every two to five years.
On top of this, it assumed that AI developments will force the rapid replacement of consumer computers, phones, and telecommunications equipment owing to the computing requirements of the new systems.
By taking this wide view of all the various types of e-waste that will be created, the BAN report projects that AI-driven equipment retirement will generate up to 13m metric tonnes per year by 2030 – a far higher estimate than a handful of previous studies.
AI datacenter construction has already created a groundswell of bipartisan opposition around the US for the huge amount of space and energy it requires, but the report comes when focus is turning to the long-term pollution AI could create.
A group of environmental and health experts last week called for the federal government to issue a pledge to protect citizens’ health from the repercussions of AI buildout. It cited estimates that the air pollution from the enormous amount of electricity generation needed for datacenters could result in hundreds of thousands of new asthma cases and as many as 1,300 premature deaths per year in the US alone.
The Trump administration has sought to weaken environmental safeguards that would normally govern such a massive technological buildout.
A 2025 report by McKinsey & Company estimates that, in order to achieve the tech industry’s planned rollout of artificial intelligence, nearly $7tn in capital outlays will be needed worldwide in the next five years to build datacenters running millions of computer servers 24 hours a day.
BAN’s white paper notes that this unprecedented spending “is roughly the cost of ending world hunger for the next 75 years – being spent in just five”.
“We all find ourselves unwitting participants in the AI horserace,” said the report, “as IT users everywhere find themselves using AI whether they would like to or not, and yet almost always, without being aware of the greater consequences of doing so.”

items.title: Repairable gadgets are becoming a genuine selling point for UK specialist retailers
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. There was a time, not so long ago, when a broken power button or a dying battery meant one thing: tossing a perfectly good piece of tech into the bin and heading down to the High Street for a replacement. Electronics were treated like disposable razor blades. They came sealed in glue, held together by […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
There was a time, not so long ago, when a broken power button or a dying battery meant one thing: tossing a perfectly good piece of tech into the bin and heading down to the High Street for a replacement. Electronics were treated like disposable razor blades. They came sealed in glue, held together by proprietary screws, and contained zero user-serviceable parts.
That throwaway mentality is finally catching up with us. The UK generates an estimated 1.6 million tonnes of electronic waste annually, making it one of the largest producers of e-waste per capita in the world. But walk through the aisles of tech shops today, and you will notice a distinct shift in how products are sold.
UK consumers are actively rejecting disposable culture. In response, specialist retailers across the country are discovering that modular, easily repairable hardware is no longer just a nice environmental perk; it is turning into one of their strongest selling points.
The shift from disposable to modular design
For years, big players in the tech world designed phones in such a way that they would become obsolete after every eighteen to twenty-four months. Batteries were stuck onto screen assemblies while simple repairs were impossible without professional tools and thermal equipment.
Today, small retailers and specialty shops see that customers need durability. It is so frustrating to pay hundreds of pounds for good-quality electronics only to find out that one faulty £5 part can make the whole device inoperable.
All this has made modular design more appealing than ever before. The products built using screw fittings, replaceable batteries, and easy-to-access inner parts convince even the most skeptical customers. It is much easier to justify the initial cost when the buyer knows that they can purchase new O-rings, batteries, or even an extra glass tube sometime in the future.
Premium hardware thrives on longevity
This phenomenon can be observed in virtually every consumer electronics category in the UK.
When it comes to personal computers, examples like the Framework laptop have shown that people are willing to spend money on devices that allow port switching, memory upgrades, and keyboard replacements using a basic screwdriver. As for home audio equipment, companies that make products with replaceable headphone pads, detachable cords, and even replaceable drivers perform much better than disposable earbuds with a built-in lithium pack.
The exact same preference for user-serviceable build quality is driving choices in small lifestyle electronics. When buyers shop for high-end dry herb portable units, seeing a device like the Tinymight 2 instantly builds confidence because it avoids a glued-shut casing in favor of solid Finnish oak, stainless steel, and a user-replaceable 18650 battery. If the cell wears down after a few hundred charge cycles, you don’t throw the device away. You simply swap in a fresh battery and keep using it.
For specialist retailers, stocking items built with this level of repairability reduces return rates and transforms one-off transactions into long-term customer relationships.
Why UK retailers are lLeaning in
Independent stores have to function under harsh conditions. The competition on price alone, with massive online markets, would spell failure. To succeed and earn money, specialized stores have to depend on know-how and product selection.
Focusing on repairable hardware gives retailers three massive commercial advantages:
- Lower Warranty Overhead: Products built with modular parts are fundamentally easier to service. If a customer experiences a minor issue, a retailer can often send out a simple replacement part rather than absorbing the cost of shipping an entire brand-new unit back and forth.
- Higher Customer Lifetime Value: A customer who buys a repairable device stays connected to the retailer. They come back to the shop over several years for official accessories, replacement seals, upgraded attachments, and fresh power cells.
- Authentic Sustainability: British consumers have become less and less convinced by corporate ‘greenwashing’. Drawing attention to tangible repairability provides evidence that an item is durable, which appeals greatly to green consumers.
The legislative push behind the trend
Preferences of consumers do not appear out of nowhere. They are being supported by policy. The UK Right to Repair laws have been expanding, forcing manufacturers to make spare parts and repair manuals available to average consumers and repair businesses.
While early legislation focused heavily on major home appliances like washing machines and refrigerators, the cultural expectation has bled into smaller personal electronics. Buyers now expect the same right to fix their own gear whether it lives in the kitchen, sits on an office desk, or travels in a jacket pocket.
Early stockists who understood this trend have been the ones to benefit from it. In keeping with their strategy of stockpiling items for maintenance purposes and not for obsolescence, they have managed to build a reputation that their rivals can never compete with.
The future of retail is built lLast
The age of taking glued-together and unserviceable electronics as the normal way of things is coming to an end. People are making their purchases based on the quality of construction, reparability, and longevity.
When considering the UK specialty retail market, emphasizing repairability engineering is not just good marketing for 2026. It is also a good business move to cultivate a loyal customer base that knows your product will endure.

items.title: Morrisons sales rise as debt-ridden grocer cuts costs
items.summary: Morrisons has toasted faster sales growth as the private-equity-owned grocer nears £1bn in savings as it races to trim its huge debt pile.  The grocer saw like-for-like sales jump by 3.2 per cent to £1.4bn in the three months to the end of July, as its chief executive attributed this “stronger sales momentum” to the [...]
items.body:
Morrisons sales rise as debt-ridden grocer cuts costs
Morrisons has toasted faster sales growth as the private-equity-owned grocer nears £1bn in savings as it races to trim its huge debt pile.
The grocer saw like-for-like sales jump by 3.2 per cent to £1.4bn in the three months to the end of July, as its chief executive attributed this “stronger sales momentum” to the summer’s record temperatures and the World Cup.
Rami Batiéh, who joined Morrisons to lead its turnaround in 2023, said the supermarket’s drastic cost-cutting regime is fuelling a “broad-based improvement” across the group.
The firm made £53m in cost savings in the three-month period, pushing its total cuts up to £995m since it kicked off its cost-cutting drive in March 2023.
Morrisons said these savings are helping the group to cut its net debt and offset “headwinds” caused by the war in Iran, which has pushed up supply costs and dampened consumer confidence.
Batiéh said: “Our stronger sales momentum reflected a broad-based improvement across the business – with our supermarkets, online, convenience, pharmacy and Myton manufacturing businesses all reporting good growth, underlining our progress with our plans to renew and modernise Morrisons.
“Key to this performance is our continued commitment to keeping prices low. The recent launch of our Unbeatables price promise, which guarantees customers won’t find better value on hundreds of essential products at named major supermarkets, has already had a positive impact.”
Last month, the grocer promised to match rival supermarkets on the price of hundreds of essential products, including bananas, bread, chicken, bacon and pizza.
The pledge turned up the heat on an emerging price war in the UK’s grocery sector, as retailers compete to prove to customers that they are not using the Iran war as an excuse to hike prices.
Morrisons said its 3.2-per-cent sales growth in the last quarter was its fifteenth consecutive period of growth.
Morrisons weighed down by debt pile
The group said it will accelerate the expansion of its Morrisons Daily convenience arm. The firm opened 71 so far this year and has plans for hundreds more in the coming years, though it has closed dozens of unprofitable convenience stores it acquired from McColl’s in 2022.
Morrisons has been grappling with a mounting debt pile since its takeover by private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) in 2021. Last year, its net debt grew from £7.1bn to £7.5bn.
The group has been forced to take drastic measures to cut this debt. It has sold the freehold rights to large parts of its property portfolio and is reportedly in talks to sell food from its Myton manufacturing business to rival supermarkets.
Morrisons said it has cut its debt mile by 46 per cent since 2022 and still owns the freehold rights to most of its supermarket estate.
Jo Goff, the group’s finance chief, said: “Cumulative cost savings now approaching £1bn helped us offset extensive external cost headwinds while also focussing on what is most important; investment in our colleagues and in stronger value for customers.
“Our working capital improvement programme continues to progress well and our confidence that there is more to come is demonstrated by our decision to raise our target today to £750m.”

items.title: Gambling giant blames job cuts on Burnham high street crackdown
items.summary: Ladbrokes owner Entain has hit out at Andy Burnham’s plans to shake up the high street as the gambling giant blamed the Prime Minister for its decision to cut 400 jobs.  The group, which also owns Coral, has announced that it will cut about a fifth of the headcount of its global customer care team, [...]
items.body:
Gambling giant blames job cuts on Burnham high street crackdown
Ladbrokes owner Entain has hit out at Andy Burnham’s plans to shake up the high street as the gambling giant blamed the Prime Minister for its decision to cut 400 jobs.
The group, which also owns Coral, has announced that it will cut about a fifth of the headcount of its global customer care team, which it said could mean around 400 jobs are lost.
Stella David, the firm’s chief executive, has blamed “a backdrop of rising costs and increasing pressure” on the gambling sector and Andy Burnham’s plans to crack down further on betting shops in his bid to revamp Britain’s high streets.
In a letter to the Prime Minister, the gambling boss warned Burnham against hiking machine games duty (MGD) from 20 to 40 per cent, which a thinktank has said could cost the sector £460m.
David said that this move would cause “substantial” job losses and shop closures across UK high streets, undermining Burnham’s attempts to boost town centres.
Burnham has vowed to crack down on betting shops and vape sellers, which he says have “hollowed out” high streets across the country.
Gambling shops part of high street fabric
The Entain boss told the Prime Minister that the firm’s gambling shops “have been part of their local communities for decades, providing jobs, supporting local economies and offering familiar, staffed places where customers meet and interact”.
She said the hike to MGD would cost Entain’s UK retail business £100m every year and threaten the group’s ability to hire young people, as the country faces a youth unemployment crisis.
“Ladbrokes and Coral betting shops are sports and racing businesses, with machine gaming only one part of a much broader offer,” she added. “They are long-established, staffed community hubs, many with roots stretching back decades in the same towns and high streets.
“A tax increase of the proposed scale would also risk pushing gambling activity away from the regulated high street rather than simply reducing it. […] The better outcome for communities and the public finances is to keep gambling within the regulated sector and, wherever possible, bring activity currently taking place illegally back into it.”
Burnham’s pledge to shake up British high streets has faced criticism from high-profile business figures, including Frasers Group founder Mike Ashley and JD Wetherspoon chairman Sir Tim Martin.
Martin told City AM last week that it is “not up to” the Prime Minister to choose which businesses are allowed to be on the high street.
Entain’s boss pointed to gambling tax hikes imposed under the government of Burnham’s predecessor, Sir Keir Starmer, which piled levies onto remote gambling.
“A further doubling of [MGD] would therefore add another significant cost to businesses already struggling to absorb major tax increases, stacking the odds against labour-intensive high-street operators and making it harder to sustain shops, jobs and investment in local communities,” David said.
An Entain spokesperson said its job cuts are “part of its ongoing efforts to address the impact of the UK’s increased gambling taxes, while also supporting our progress in becoming a sharper, fitter and more agile business”.
Shares in the group, which was demoted from the FTSE 100 to the FTSE 250 earlier this month, lost about 0.7 per cent to 494p on Wednesday morning.
