3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.

TransactionTree hires industry veteran Peter Ingram as it plots convenience and fuel retail expansion
AI powered retail operations platform TransactionTree has appointed Peter Ingram as Senior Vice President of Strategy and Partnerships. He comes onboard to lead the company’s expansion into the convenience and fuel retail sector.
Ingram has spent more than 25 years in the convenience and fuel space’s technology stack - Point of Sale, back office, fuel systems, loyalty, payments, and the integrations between them that rarely work as advertised. His career spans retail technology, FinTech, marketing and sales, covering strategy, business development, corporate development and operations.
“There is no shortage of dashboards in this industry,” Ingram says. “What’s missing is a trusted, real-time record - one that can tell an associate what to do in the next three minutes and tell the region and the home office the same thing at the same time. The back office isn’t really a place anymore. The business is wherever the shopper is. That’s the problem I came here to work on.”
“Retailers are sitting on their most valuable asset and using a fraction of it,” says Kevin Saum, CEO at TransactionTree (pictured below). “The transaction is the most complete and most honest record a retailer owns. Worse than underusing it, though, is what’s happening now - companies are putting an AI layer on top of siloed data. The AI sees one system’s slice, on one refresh schedule, and answers with total confidence. That isn’t a view of your enterprise. It’s several confident answers that don’t reconcile.”
He adds: “The work is making the entire record real-time and trusted first. Peter has spent 25 years watching this industry try to skip that step.”

items.title: Mike Ashley’s Frasers faces shareholder revolt over exec bonus
items.summary: Frasers Group, the retail empire owned by Mike Ashley, is facing an investor revolt over a bonus handed to its finance chief for “doing his job”.  Two influential shareholder proxies have urged the firm’s investors to slap down its executives’ pay package at its annual general meeting (AGM) on Thursday.  The dispute centres around a [...]
items.body:
Mike Ashley’s Frasers faces shareholder revolt over exec bonus
Frasers Group, the retail empire owned by Mike Ashley, is facing an investor revolt over a bonus handed to its finance chief for “doing his job”.
Two influential shareholder proxies have urged the firm’s investors to slap down its executives’ pay package at its annual general meeting (AGM) on Thursday.
The dispute centres around a £100,000 bonus handed to Chris Wootton, the firm’s finance chief, earlier this year.
Frasers said the finance boss deserved the reward because of his successful negotiating of a new loan and revolving credit facility for the company. The loan deal is worth £3bn and will last until July 2029.
“The committee’s view was that this was a significant objective in the continued delivery of our elevation strategy,” the firm said in its annual report. But the shareholder advisory groups have taken issue with the bonus, which they say rewards Wootton for an achievement that should be treated as part of his normal role.
ISS, one top shareholder group, told investors: “The decision to award a discretionary bonus outside the standard framework is questionable, as the accomplishment appears to sit comfortably within a CFO’s normal remit and day-to-day job description.”
Glass Lewis, another leading investor proxy, said Frasers should have given shareholders a “more robust disclosure regarding the rationale for the award”.
The proxy pointed out that the firm did not meet the threshold for its performance-related long-term bonuses to be triggered last year, suggesting that Frasers used this one-off bonus to “prop up pay” regardless.
Pay packets under the scope
Wootton took £351,000 in salary, pension and short-term bonuses last year, while the group’s chief operating officer, David Al-Mudallal, took home £251,000.
Michael Murray, Frasers Group’s chief executive and founder Mike Ashley’s son-in-law, has waived his salary.
Proxy advisers have faced the City’s anger in recent years for campaigning against executives’ pay packets, which some have argued are already too low to attract the world’s top talent.
Ashley founded Frasers Group as Sports Direct in 1982, and it gained market dominance for selling sportswear at rock-bottom prices. But the retail tycoon and former Newcastle United owner has since begun a march into upmarket fashion with his luxury label Flannels.
The group snapped up struggling department store chain Harvey Nichols for about £40m last month and is seeking to gain control of Hugo Boss, a German fashion house.
Frasers Group declined to comment.

items.body:
Ferrero launches an all-new range of much-anticipated Wonka products, created with the expertise of its UK Research & Development team and manufacturing colleagues in Alfreton, Derbyshire.
The launch marks a significant innovation milestone for Ferrero UK. Drawing on decades of confectionery expertise and investment in its Alfreton Centre of Excellence, Ferrero has brought together research, product development, innovation and manufacturing capabilities to create products rooted in the company’s signature standards of quality, creativity and craftsmanship. The new Wonka range combines local UK expertise with Ferrero’s global capabilities, helping to deliver imaginative products to consumers in the UK, Ireland and other markets around the world.
“This launch is a proud moment for Ferrero in the UK. Our Alfreton team has played a key role in bringing the new Wonka range to life, combining deep confectionery expertise with the creativity, craft and technical capability needed to reimagine such an iconic brand for today’s consumers,” said Craig Barker, managing director, Ferrero UK and Ireland.
“The fact that products developed with UK expertise will be enjoyed by consumers in the UK, Ireland and other markets around the world speaks to the strength of our people, our manufacturing capability and our continued investment in innovation here in Derbyshire. Wonka is a brand built on imagination and wonder, and our teams have worked hard to translate that spirit into products that deliver the quality, surprise and delight consumers expect from Ferrero.”
Over the last decade, Ferrero has invested more than £35 million in the Alfreton site, helping to modernise its capabilities, expand production and establish it as a Centre of Excellence for assortments and model figures for the Ferrero Group.
The site’s unique manufacturing capabilities reflect decades of craftsmanship that have been leveraged to bring the new Wonka range to life. Every new Wonka product combines manufacturing excellence with research and development creativity, bringing surprising nostalgic flavours and imaginative formats to consumers.
The range includes Wonka Magic Hats, Wonka Oompa Loompa Milk Chocolate Hollow Figurines, Wonka Purplypurple Milk Chocolate Bar, Wonka Magic Garden Ropes, Wonka Oompa Loompa Gummies and a Wonka Kinder Joy Egg. Products first arrive in Morrisons and Asda from 14 September, before rolling out across other major UK and Ireland retailers, including Tesco from 22 October.
“My team and I are incredibly proud that our Alfreton team in Derbyshire has played such a pivotal role in the innovation and manufacturing for Ferrero Group on the global launch of the new Wonka range. Wonka is hugely nostalgic and has existed for generations, so we looked at familiar flavours many people will remember from when they were younger and brought them to life in unexpected new ways. Across the range, our goal was to combine nostalgic flavours with imaginative chocolate experiences, creating the sense of surprise and wonder that is synonymous with Wonka.
“Close collaboration between our Alfreton manufacturing team and global colleagues has been instrumental in delivering products that capture the creativity, quality and sense of wonder at the heart of the Wonka brand. For example, Magic Hats combine Alfreton’s chocolate-making heritage with imaginative Wonka-inspired flavours and distinctive decoration, from the fizz of popping candy to refined praline fillings and rich hazelnut notes that are iconic to Ferrero. Developing this range has been about balancing creativity with technical excellence, while staying true to Ferrero’s standards of quality, craftsmanship and great taste.” said Gary Youren, Head of R&D, Ferrero UK and Ireland.
Barker concludes: “This launch demonstrates exactly what continued investment in UK innovation and manufacturing can deliver. By combining the creativity and technical expertise of our Alfreton team with Ferrero’s global brand-building capabilities, we are able to bring distinctive products to market, while delivering the quality and taste experience consumers expect from Ferrero. It is a powerful example of how our UK business is helping to shape innovation for consumers here and around the world.”

items.title: Amazon invests over $230M in benefits, pay for Whole Foods store employees
items.summary: As the company continues to merge its operations with the specialty grocer, this next investment focuses on its frontline workers.
items.body:
Dive Brief:
- Amazon is investing more than $230 million to provide Whole Foods Market team members with higher pay, expanded benefits and new programs supporting their health and families, the company announced late last week.
- Beginning Sept. 28, hourly workers will get compensation increases “with predictable [pay] increases each year,” the company said. Starting Jan. 1, the specialty grocer’s workers will gain access to Amazon’s comprehensive benefits.
- These changes mark the latest in a series of moves by Amazon to align Whole Foods more closely with its operations and employee structure.
Dive Insight:
Amazon said the average total compensation for Whole Foods’ store workers is increasing to more than $29 an hour when factoring in the new benefits, and that the total value of benefits for full-time employees is increasing by more than 75%.
At the start of next year, eligible full-time employees will begin receiving comprehensive health plans that provide access to primary care and behavioral health providers with $5 copays. Eligible plans include a One Medical membership with same-day and virtual doctor visits at no added cost, according to the press release. Nearly 20,000 part-time employees will gain access to dental and vision coverage and free basic life insurance.
Amazon noted team members covering a family or managing ongoing health needs “stand to see the most meaningful savings.”
Company-paid short- and long-term disability insurance will begin automatically at no cost, and when workers enroll in an Amazon medical plan, they will gain fertility and family-building care as well as cancer support and care navigation. Fully paid parental leave will also be available, with up to 20 weeks for birthing parents and up to six weeks for supporting and adoptive parents.
Every hourly Whole Foods employee will also get a free Amazon Prime membership, low-cost prescriptions through Amazon Pharmacy and other savings in addition to their existing 20% in-store discount benefit.
Career Choice, Amazon’s education benefit that prepays tuition for college, skills training and certifications, will also become available to Whole Foods staffers next year.
Since mid-2025, Amazon has been working to unify its leadership and integrate its benefits with Whole Foods. In June 2025, the company restructured its Worldwide Grocery division to add Whole Foods executives. A few months later, Amazon set a deadline of December 2026 to bring corporate Whole Foods employees under the same benefits program and compensation structure as Amazon corporate workers.

items.summary: The group behind US gaming giant Roblox is suing a UK food brand and its philanthropic arm over alleged intellectual property infringement. Roblox Corporation, the Californian video game developer, filed a lawsuit in the London High Court on Friday against Roc Co, a British grocery business, and its charity arm, according to filings seen by City [...]
items.body:
Gaming platform Roblox sues British charity
The group behind US gaming giant Roblox is suing a UK food brand and its philanthropic arm over alleged intellectual property infringement.
Roblox Corporation, the Californian video game developer, filed a lawsuit in the London High Court on Friday against Roc Co, a British grocery business, and its charity arm, according to filings seen by City AM.
Roc Co Brands is a for-profit food manufacturer, established in May 2020 by a British family and named after their son, Rocco, who survived a severe medical crisis at birth.
The lawsuit also names its charity arm, Rocco Brands Group. The charity donates all net trading profits from Rocco Brands Group sales to healthcare and childhood sickness charities, including the NHS and Ronald McDonald House Charities UK. Its website stated it has raised £15,000 for charity over the past 12 months.
The case was filed in the Intellectual Property and Enterprise Court, a specialist court within the High Court, with law firm Winston Taylor representing the blocky playground platform. Through the UK Intellectual Property Office, Roblox Corporation holds active trademarks, including its name and logo.
It is understood that one of the products the British brand recently released was Rocblox Confectionery, a collection of sour cable sweets in packages featuring robot characters on a blocky background. This case concerns Roblox seeking to defend its trademarks and IP from alleged unauthorised misuse.
Businesses or charities can obtain a license to use the Roblox logo and brand trademarks, but it is understood that Roc Co was not granted such a license in this case.
It is also understood that this lawsuit is not about money, and if the gaming giant succeeds, any money recovered through these proceedings will be donated to one of the three independent charitable organisations listed on the Roc Co website.
Roblox Corporation, Roc Co Brands, and Winston Taylor were contacted for comment.

items.title: 'Stop hammering Middle England': Jigsaw owner slams Labour tax hikes
items.summary: David Ross, the owner of Jigsaw, told the Daily Mail Labour needs to stop hitting Middle England's income via frozen tax thresholds and higher costs and taxes.
items.body:
'Stop hammering Middle England': Jigsaw owner slams Labour tax hikes
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
The boss of upmarket fashion retailer Jigsaw has urged Andy Burnham to ‘stop hammering Middle England’ as tax hikes weigh on spending.
David Ross, who bought Jigsaw in 2018, urged the Prime Minister to reverse tax increases and make it a ‘fair deal’ for businesses and employees.
‘The system is currently stacked against retailers and our customers,’ he said. ‘We will see whether Andy Burnham is genuine about reviving Britain’s high streets.’
The entrepreneur, who co-founded Carphone Warehouse, said the Government had to ‘stop hammering Middle England. Our customer works, pays her taxes, and has watched frozen thresholds and higher bills eat her pay rise.
‘Very often she’s also the person behind the till. Squeeze her and you squeeze the shop, the jobs and the tax take together. Leave working households’ take home pay alone.’
Rising labour and energy costs, paired with changes to business rates, have hammered businesses, and there are mounting fears that there’s more to come in next month’s Budget, as Chancellor John Healey grapples with limited headroom and a pledge to increase spending on welfare and defence.
Ross called on Burnham to reform business rates and ‘keep shops out of the new top that was aimed at warehouses and hit flagship stores instead.’
Jigsaw owner David Ross is calling on Burnham to reform business rates
He joins other retailers in calling for the threshold for employers’ National Insurance to be upped to £6,000, adding that changes to workers’ rights should target exploitative practices or contracts rather than flexible jobs.
‘Youth unemployment is at a ten-year high, don’t let new employment rules kill the Saturday job, where millions of us learned the value of hard work. Target the exploitative contracts and leave the weekend jobs alone.’
He added: 'None of this is a handout. It's a fair deal for the businesses that create jobs and the people who do them. Give us a chance, Andy.'
Ross’s comments came as Jigsaw claimed its ‘turnaround is working’ after an 18 per cent increase in sales in the six months to July, compared to a year earlier.
It was driven by a 43 per cent jump in dress sales, and its yellow suit, launched in March, sold out within three weeks.
Concession sales, where Jigsaw products are sold in sites like department stores, jumped by 47 per cent on a like-for-like basis year-on-year, while online sales increased by 21 per cent.
The business said international online sales increased by 48 per cent year-on-year in the period. It plans to push further into the US via Macy's and Nordstrom's online marketplaces from this autumn.
That came despite a ‘subdued market backdrop’ as retailers absorb higher costs, with ‘little targeted support for business’ ahead of the Budget on October 28.
Jigsaw hailed its recent progress after launching a turnaround programme to help improve its performance after recording a £3.5million loss for the year to March 2025.
Making a stand: Sales at Jigsaw are on the up and shoppers are loving the chain's dresses
Its 'strategic reset', started in 2025, has focused on strengthening its core business in Britain, upping its international reach and creating 'authority and consistency' across its product lines.
Tikki Godley, managing director of Jigsaw, said: 'This season is further evidence that our turnaround is working.
'Customers are watching their wallets right now, but still choosing Jigsaw.’
In March, the group said it planned to open 10 new shops across Britain this year.
Founded in 1970, luxury womenswear retailer Jigsaw has long been synonymous with timeless tailoring and quality craftsmanship. But in a market crowded with fast fashion and hyper-digitised retail, it has had to evolve rapidly.
The business struggled during the Covid-19 pandemic to retain its middle-class shopper base and was forced to close 30 shops.
Jonathan De Mello, founder of JDM Retail, said: 'While high street pressures, flat non-food retail markets, and rising business costs remain persistent challenges, Jigsaw has managed to shrug these off with good growth across all channels, driven by a surge in dress sales in particular.
‘The future prognosis is encouraging as the brand pivots from stabilisation to international growth, with a forthcoming US launch this autumn via Nordstrom and Macy’s.’

Launching initially in Sainsbury’s from 5 September, the range will include four SKUs: Signature 10 Collection, Recipe Collection, Tropical Paradise Collection and Farmers’ Market Collection, bringing Jelly Belly’s distinctive flavour-led proposition to supermarket shelves in a new premium sharing format.
Previously available primarily through specialist confectionery stores, online and department stores, the move into grocery will significantly increase the brand’s accessibility, creating an opportunity for retailers to convert existing recognition into trial and sales.
The new range launches with a premium, resealable pouch format, designed to deliver stand-out on shelf and capitalise on sharing occasions.
Jo Harwood, chief sales and trade marketing officer at FBC, said: “Being named as UK distribution partner for Jelly Belly is a significant move for FBC. It’s a brand with genuine global fame and huge existing UK awareness, but no UK-wide grocery presence to match.
“We think shoppers are going to love discovering it properly for the first time with some exciting flavour combinations, and there’s huge opportunity for retailers to drive trial and incremental sales as a result.
“Unlike chocolate confectionery, we believe sugar confectionery is a massively under-premiumised market in the UK. Jelly Belly’s gourmet experience can unlock this potential, offering exciting trading up opportunities for retailers.”
While 100g bags will RRP at £2.30 at supermarkets, a smaller 28g format (RRP 90p) has also been launched to unlock impulse and wholesale channels.

items.title: M&S to sell bags of extra bakery items for under £4 in partnership with Too Good To Go
items.summary: M&S Food will offer bags of food to customers for less than £4 as it rolls out its partnership with Too Good To Go across the country.
items.body:
M&S to sell bags of extra bakery items for under £4 in partnership with Too Good To Go
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
M&S Food will offer bags of food to customers for less than £4 as it rolls out its partnership with Too Good To Go across the country.
Shoppers will be able to buy the surprise bags, which contain three to four bakery items worth a minimum of £10.20, at the end of the day from across 350 M&S stores.
The bags, which cost £3.80, can be ordered through the Too Good To Go app from Monday to Saturday, one hour before the store closes.
The nationwide rollout follows a trial in a select number of M&S stores over the past few months.
Lucinda Langton, head of sustainability at M&S Food, said: 'Too Good To Go is a brilliant example of how we're turning our commitment to reducing food waste into practical action.
'By giving customers access to surprise bags of surplus bakery products, we can help ensure more of our food is enjoyed. The response from our trial stores has been outstanding, and this partnership is another positive step towards our goal of halving food waste by 2030.'
Too good to go: M&S will sell surprise bags for under £4 in a bid to cut food waste
The Too Good To Go app, founded in 2015, connects customers with shops and restaurants that have extra food available.
Brands such as Greggs and Pret have already partnered with the app, as well as supermarkets Aldi and Morrison's.
The company claims to have helped save over 600million meals from going to waste, boasting 120million registered users and 200,000 partners across 20 countries.
Chelsea Kerr, managing director at Too Good To Go UK & Ireland, said: 'We're delighted to be partnering with M&S to help make their surplus food available to even more customers across the UK and Ireland.
'Food waste is a huge challenge, but partnerships like this show how simple it can be for businesses and consumers to take action together.
'By giving food that might otherwise go unsold another chance to be enjoyed, we're making it easier for people to save good food while also getting great value.
'M&S is a much-loved brand across the UK, so we're excited to be working together to make saving food from going to waste a simple and accessible part of everyday life for even more people.'
Availability of the bags will be limited and will vary daily depending on the store.

items.title: Packed lunch revival boosts demand for meal prep staples, data shows
items.summary: Office professionals are sparking a major packed lunch revival. Driven by rising costs, workers across the country are swapping store-bought lunches for homemade creations to stretch their budgets further, new supermarket data reveals. Data from online supermarket Ocado highlights a clear shift in consumer habits.… This story continues at Packed lunch revival boosts demand for meal prep staples, data shows Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Data from online supermarket Ocado highlights a clear shift in consumer habits.
Searches for “lunch bowls” are up 79% year-on-year, alongside strong growth in meal prep staples like microwavable rice (+23% year-on-year) and ziplock bags (+60% year-on-year)
Nearly half of UK professionals (46%) now bring a packed lunch to work more frequently than they did a year ago.
The push is largely financial: seven in 10 (69%) say that buying lunch near the office has become too expensive, while 72% say bringing food from home helps them better manage household finances.
Nutrition is another core driver, with two-thirds (66%) noting that packed lunches make it easier to eat healthily and track macros or calories.
And social media is accelerating the shift. Content creators like Frankie Parker (161,000 Instagram followers) regularly share lunchbox ideas as 61% of workers turn online for inspiration.
Although traditional sandwiches remain popular (52%), Ocado shoppers are increasingly seeking out more inspired options, with searches soaring for salad bowls (+100%), pasta salad (+24%), and grain bowls (+173%).
Convenient grab-and-go lunchbox snacks are also thriving. With searches for lunchbox snacks spiking 79% and sales of Babybel having risen by 34% on Ocado.
This shift is being driven by younger generations establishing long-term habits, with a quarter of Gen Z and Millennial employees (25%) saying they bring a homemade lunch every day they are in the office and 64% of this demographic admitting they bring their lunch to work more often than they did last year.
Dan Elton, chief customer officer at Ocado Retail, commented: “Consumers are looking for smart, practical ways to save money, embracing packed lunches as part of their routine to curb everyday on-the-go spending.
“Our search trends show there is a clear demand for affordable, inspiring options amongst our customers. From grab and go lunchbox staples to nutritious salad bowls and a variety of ingredients that make batch-cook lunch prep easy, Ocado is helping shoppers get more from their lunchboxes whatever their budget or taste.”

items.body:
It is now open to the public serving a wide selection of Co-op brand lines as well as other popular convenience goods.
Located on St John’s Road in the Cheshire town, the new store has benefited from a full fit out of the new Nisa proposition from its previous fascia. Standing at 1,500sqft, the new store is the third Nisa store for business owner Martin Corban.
Corban will operate the store serving the bustling residential area with vital food for now, on the go food and drink solutions, snacks, treats, BWS, fresh, produce and more.
The new store gives local shoppers access to a wide range of everyday essentials, fresh food and Co-op brand products, offering them quality, value and convenience.
Among the Co-op brand lines available to all Nisa symbols to stock are fresh and chilled, food-to-go, fresh produce, frozen and award-winning premium ranges, under the Irresistible moniker.
Holly Perry, key account manager at Co-op Wholesale, commented: “We’re really pleased to be opening this store with Martin and team as partners.
“It is in a superb location and is set up to trade well, serve the community and make a brilliant retail business. We wish the team the very best of luck and are certain it will go from strength to strength.”
Martin Corban, owner of Nisa Congleton, commented: “Opening our Nisa store in Congleton marks a really exciting time – we’ve long admired all that comes with being part of the Co-op Wholesale group, including access to the Co-op brand lines, the outstanding expertise and support and the highly recognisable Nisa symbol.
“The town is undergoing significant housing development meaning quality convenience stores provide a much-needed amenity.
“We’ve received excellent support from the Co-op Wholesale team and are looking forward to working with them as we grow our business and service this town and beyond.”
As part of the launch, £500 has been donated, via Co-op Wholesale’s charity Making A Difference Locally (MADL), to The Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation – a foundation set up to help children and young adults in need, in and around the local area, as well as charities supporting those affected by road traffic deaths.
Kate Carroll, Social Value Lead said: “The Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation is a charity close to the hearts of the team at Nisa Congleton and was chosen to receive £500 from MADL as part of the launch celebrations.
“The Foundation was created in memory of Georgia ‘Gee’ Ogden and is a powerful example of turning tragedy into hope for others. The donation will support the Foundation’s work helping children and young adults in need, as well as those affected by road traffic fatalities.
“We wish the charity every success as it continues to honour Gee’s memory through positive action in local communities.”

items.title: Riverford founder: How I went from 50p bags of carrots to building a £117M a year organic veg box business
items.summary: We speak to Guy Singh-Watson, who tells us how he started and grew his organic veg box company Riverford, in our new How We Built It series.
items.body:
Riverford founder: How I went from 50p bags of carrots to building a £117M a year organic veg box business
- We speak to Guy Singh-Watson in our new How We Built It series
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Guy Singh-Watson, 66, still has some of the old hoes and seed drills he used to plant, then pick the first leeks at his fledgling business 40 years ago.
A decades-old tractor called ‘the beast’ that a local mechanic now refuses to mend sits in the corner of a field at his Devon firm’s sprawling HQ.
The old tools and machinery may now stand still, but organic vegetable box company Riverford continues to plough on.
At a time when supermarkets and their suppliers are under pressure to cut costs further, it seems there is still appetite for smaller-scale companies to sell directly to customers.
Riverford boxes of organic vegetables start at £20 and are delivered to 70,000 customers a week. Its turnover last year rose 6 per cent to £117 million.
So does Singh-Watson, who was plain Guy Watson before marrying gastropub entrepreneur Geetie Singh in 2014, ever get nostalgic?
He smiles: ‘Sometimes I think how on earth did this all happen? I meet people in the pub I paid 50p for a bag of carrots in the 1980s or remember my first child buried in artichoke seeds as I pushed down a pram planting them every metre.'
Guy Singh-Watson founded Riverford in the mid-1980s before the organic boom took off
The seeds for Riverford were planted when in 1985, he returned to his parents’ farm, where they had been primarily dairy and livestock farmers since the early 1950s.
Quitting a career in management consultancy, he planted the first three acres and began growing organic vegetables a year later.
When he started, Singh-Watson would pull up the vegetables and by 9 o’clock they were at greengrocers in local towns, while he also sold produce from the back of his Citroen 2CV in Totnes.
In 1987 he launched Riverford and ‘extraordinary growth’ then came in the late 1990s as organic became aspirational. But there have been hurdles to negotiate, not least when he progressed to selling to organic wholesalers in London.
‘They robbed me blind,’ he recalls. ‘One took all my one-year profits, declared himself bankrupt and was trading somewhere else the next day.’
Singh-Watson says that as a naive Devon farm boy this was an ‘eye-opener’, adding: ‘As I got more worldly wise. I was determined I’d never treat another human being with the ritualistic contempt of how a supermarket buyer treats farmers.’
Twenty years after launching, Riverford had garnered around £30million in sales at a time when the UK was one of the largest markets in Europe.
Singh-Watson has campaigned for supermarkets to treat farmers fairly and improve buying
He sold 74 per cent of his Riverford shares to an employee trust in 2018 and before selling his final stake in 2023 for £9.8 million he wrote Riverford’s supplier charter, in which he vows not to replicate the ‘wasteful and abusive’ relationships he had with supermarket buyers.
‘I would like to see supermarkets copy it,’ he says. ‘The world would be a better place if those relationships were humane.’
Riverford is now fully owned by its more than 1,000 employees and is one of the UK’s most significant examples of employee ownership.
He says that ‘for the most part it’s been an absolute success’, adding: ‘Giving a larger number of people a say has helped us make better decisions and consult more widely. The best decisions are when you look at a problem from many angles.
‘If you have people with many views and backgrounds they are more able to do it than a board.’
Singh-Watson has been a campaigner since taking the Government to court in 1999 over genetically modified crops. He is outspoken on intensive farming practices and is spearheading a UK campaign to ban weedkiller glyphosate during harvest time.
‘I am a controversial figure,’ he admits. ‘I’m in favour of farmers paying inheritance tax – it didn’t make me many friends locally.’
Yet he wants to see farming thrive, especially mixed smaller farms, and says Riverford has made a significant contribution.
‘Quite a number of our suppliers wouldn’t be in business today without Riverford,’ he says. ‘It’s a source of immense pride.’
Singh-Watson takes great pride in customer relationships too, saying: ‘Trust at Riverford has been built up over 40 years. A lot of people come by recommendation and word of mouth.
‘If you are asking people to pay a third more for their food, they have to believe that you are doing things in a better way.’
Riverford supplies its veg boxes to households around Britain and is now employee-owned
How we built it: Quick questions
Best business advice?
Really know your customer. For us it's understanding how they cook their vegetables, what works for the kitchen, what their children are eating and where your product or service fits into their lives.
Biggest mistake?
I am a farmyard philosopher and have probably been a bit too guided. I'm glad that the world I want to live in has driven a lot of decisions as opposed to what is most commercially savvy.
First leadership lesson?
John, my first employee who still manages our farms, once said to me: 'What you have to understand is that not everyone is like you and thank God!' I was much younger, tremendously driven and probably couldn't understand why people couldn't pick leeks as fast as me. And John was absolutely right.
Biggest challenge?
My own ignorance about farming organically, while I didn't know about growing vegetables other than what was grown in my mother's garden.
I had to figure it out myself visiting other organic growers in the UK. I used to go to the Netherlands a lot where they were very welcoming and where the community is still just that.
The Riverford Cookbook: Easy Evenings will be published on October 1

items.body:
Thai Trade London, Department of International Trade Promotion (DITP) announces an inaugural collaboration with Ocado.com, to showcase 15 new products within a dedicated “Taste of Thailand” shop-in-shop on the successful retail platform. The launch of the shop this Autumn (Friday 11th September) witnesses the new additions joining the 50-plus products already available on the Ocado.com website.
The portfolio features ambient and refrigerated meal essentials including authentic curry pastes, high-grade Thai Jasmine rice and premium cooking sauces that empower the home cook, affording the confidence to deliver a Taste of Thailand culinary masterpieces from scratch.
The move to establish the Taste of Thailand shop is in line with Ocado Retail’s commitment to capitalising on the growing interest in international cuisine thanks to food tourism and the contribution made by social media and digital content to raise awareness of country-of-origin dishes. This, combined with the established appeal of Thai cuisine and the UK’s adventurous cooks’ dedication to sourcing premium, best in class global ingredients are the catalysts behind the new Taste of Thailand collection. The range prioritises access to authentic products, rather than westernised alternatives to enable the recreation of Thailand’s rich repertoire of regional cooking classics.
Thai Trade London, DITP is viewing the UK as a key focus market, anticipating a 2% (value) growth rate in the year ahead with sales projected to reach around £600k. This prediction is based on UK consumer interest in seeking out bold, authentic flavours, and the popularity of the sweet, sour, salty and spicy notes, which are the hallmark of vibrant Thai cuisine. This is alongside the broader shift in UK shopping habits, with more consumers cooking from scratch at home and actively seeking out international cuisines for weeknight meals (not just special occasions) and Thai cuisine remaining a firm favourite amongst top international food choices has further fuelled the decision to invest in building a stronger connection between Thai food culture and British consumers.
The shop-in-shop launch supported by Thai Trade London DITP, Ministry of Commerce Thailand and the participating brands is being supported by a PR and social media campaign (which includes the creation of a series of inspirational recipes showcasing the products and the pivotal role they play in delivering a diverse range of authentic Thai dishes), in addition to a programme of dedicated influencer partnerships. Promotional and media spend with Ocado.com direct is being handled by individual brands, providing them with the freedom to tailor any promotional investment in line with specific commercial priorities and budgetary considerations.
Commenting on the launch, Mr. Jirakarn Bejrajati Minister (Commercial) The Office of Commercial Affairs, Royal Thai Embassy London says, “This represents an exciting milestone for the Thai food and drink category. We are keen to promote the versatility of these products – which goes far beyond the creation of some of the much-loved traditional comfort dishes associated with Thai cuisine -, by demonstrating how to embrace the bold, punchy flavours, fresh herbs and aromatics associated with our culture, to conjure up dishes that are a genuine pleasure to cook and eat. We hope to shift Thai dishes away from simply special “treat” occasions into fresh, vibrant and relevant weekday mealtime menu choices.
With Thai Trade London, DITP backing the shop and its storytelling, and brands investing directly in their own retail visibility, we believe we are providing the range with the strongest possible foundation for long-term success.
Ocado.com is the natural retailer of choice for this collaboration, given its reputation for quality, its established engaged and discerning customer base, and strength as a platform for introducing premium and authentic international ranges to UK shoppers. Ocado Retail’s online format also allows us to tell the story behind each product clearly, helping customers understand the provenance and authenticity of what they’re buying, which is a key component of our launch strategy.”

items.body:
Knorr, one of the UK’s best-loved stock brands, is set to transform the stock category with the launch of its first-ever liquid concentrated stock. Available in Chicken and Beef flavours, the innovative Knorr Concentrated Stock range is designed to effortlessly elevate everyday cooking, providing a rich, slow-simmered flavour in a modern, convenient format.
The launch sees Knorr bring its trusted taste and culinary credibility into the fast-growing liquid stock space, which has grown +79% in value year-on-year. Demand has been driven by shoppers increasingly looking to cook from scratch at home or use a mix of prepared and unprepared ingredients to make quick and cost-effective meals while reducing food waste. Knorr Concentrated Stock taps into this need, providing an accessible, premium option for modern home cooks to enhance the flavour of their dishes.
The key innovation lies in the controllable squeezy dosing, giving home cooks the freedom and convenience to use as much or as little as required for a variety of meals from pasta sauces to soups and curries. The transparent, recyclable bottle stays fresh for up to two months in the fridge after opening, offering strong value and reducing waste. The Chicken variant has already received industry recognition, having been shortlisted in the Cooking Sauces & Pastes category at The Grocer New Product Awards 2026.
Laura Iliffe, marketing manager at Unilever, said: “Liquid stocks are driving phenomenal growth in the category, as shoppers increasingly look for speed, flexibility, and precision in the kitchen without compromising on flavour. Knorr Concentrated Stock meets this need perfectly, providing a versatile and easy-to-use format that can elevate a variety of dishes.
“For retailers, this launch presents a major opportunity to drive trade-up while expanding the reach of the liquid stock segment. By combining Knorr’s familiar brand trust with a premium format, we’re making liquid stock an appealing, accessible option for mainstream shoppers. With consumers becoming more experimental in the kitchen, we anticipate that the flexibility of the format will unlock new cooking occasions and drive significantly higher usage frequency, bringing incremental sales to the category and providing more choice for shoppers.”
The launch marks the next chapter of Knorr’s campaign partnership with brand ambassador, Fred Sirieix. As the face of the masterbrand’s “Flavour Unlocked” campaign, Fred’s familiar presence will help introduce the new “Squeeze. Stir. Done.” format to shoppers, building on the trust and momentum of his previous work with the brand. The campaign will be backed by shopper marketing and social activity starting in October, ahead of a major TV campaign returning in early 2027.
Knorr Concentrated Stock will be rolling out in the grocery channel from mid-September 2026.

items.title: Food and drink manufacturers lead push for world-first healthy food sales reporting

Five leading UK food and drink manufacturers have stepped up to introduce healthy food sales reporting from next year, ahead of any mandatory requirement. In a letter to the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, some of the UK’s largest food and drink businesses have pledged to publish healthy food sales data and […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Five leading UK food and drink manufacturers have stepped up to introduce healthy food sales reporting from next year, ahead of any mandatory requirement.
In a letter to the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care, some of the UK’s largest food and drink businesses have pledged to publish healthy food sales data and called on government to work with industry to implement a mandatory reporting system for all food and drink businesses in this parliament. They are Carlsberg Britvic, Danone North Europe, KP Snacks, Nomad Foods and Premier Foods plc.
The move would make the UK the first country in the world to introduce mandatory healthy food sales reporting across the food system and provide a consistent, transparent way of tracking progress towards healthier diets.
Karen Betts, chief executive, The Food and Drink Federation, said:”We share the government’s ambition to improve diets across the country, and we believe that the data and transparency that reporting will bring will incentivise companies to double down on progress, and give government a valuable tool to measure the impact of health policies.
“Food and drink manufacturers have a strong track record of making everyday foods better for us, and we’re determined to keep that progress going. That’s why we’re not waiting for regulation, but starting to report now on data that companies already hold. In this way, this group of early-movers can test the best ways to collate and report data to support our broader sector and government in informing any future legislation.”
Richard Hall, vice president general secretary, Danone North Europe, said: “At Danone, we believe transparency is one of the best ways to drive progress on health and have long chosen to go beyond mandatory health and nutrition reporting requirements. We welcome this group, which will play an important role in driving greater transparency and consistency in the wider food system. The more we collectively measure and share, the easier it is to see what’s working, where barriers remain and the opportunities to accelerate progress towards better health outcomes.”
Nick Brown, Director of Environment, Social and Governance, Premier Foods, said: “Food companies can play a major role in improving the health credentials of the products they make and sell, from launching new healthier products, evolving existing recipes to make them healthier and being responsible about how we market and sell our products.
“Through disclosure, we have the opportunity to demonstrate the progress we are making and where further progress can be achieved, which is why we are proud to have already disclosed against metrics aligned to the UK Government’s Food Data Transparency Partnership”
The signatories underscore that to meet this rapid timescale, manufacturers will need to use the current Nutrient Profiling Model, which is used for existing High Fat, Sugar and Salt restrictions. This is because the complexities associated with the more recent Model would mean they’d need to develop a new set of measurements which would delay reporting.
See the letter:
Dear Secretary of State,
Supporting healthier diets by delivering mandatory healthy food sales reporting
Food and drink manufacturers share your ambition to help British people follow healthier diets and to reduce obesity.
Our industry has invested hundreds of millions of pounds here in the UK to develop healthier food and drink. As a result, our members’ products now contain 19% less sugar, 18% less salt and 17% fewer calories than they did five years ago, and this builds on steady progress since the early 2000s to reduce fat, salt and sugar and increase fruit, vegetables and fibre in everyday food and drink that people regularly enjoy.
Businesses have made these recipe changes alongside embedding the recent restrictions on the promotion and advertising of products designated as ‘Less Healthy’ (HFSS). While it’s early days for the HFSS regulations, initial evidence suggests that they are having a positive effect on consumer purchasing. Research from the University of Leeds found that sales of ‘Less Healthy’ foods fell by 2 million a day from 2021 to 2023.
We believe that the introduction of mandatory healthy food sales reporting for all large food and drink businesses is critical to support this progress. It will provide consistent data and evidence to inform future policymaking, as well as an incentive to encourage continued investment in healthier food and drink across industry.
To demonstrate our commitment and to support government in driving this forward, the companies listed below will begin voluntarily publishing healthy food sales data from next year – ahead of any mandatory requirements. These leading manufacturers, which represent some of the UKs best loved brands, are committed to sharing their experiences of introducing reporting, the pitfalls and the watchouts, to help other companies adopt the approach and to support government in designing a system that is both robust and workable at scale within this parliament.
Reporting by these companies will be based on the current Nutrient Profiling Model score – the model which underpins the HFSS regulations. Using this model will enable industry to achieve reporting at pace as it is already implemented into business systems and does not require new methodologies to be agreed with government. Food and Drink Federation Page 2
There is ambition to introduce reporting across food and drink manufacturing, and we look forward to building this initiative further as we welcome more companies and other parts of the food system into it. We expect the number of early adopters to grow as manufacturers iron out complex challenges, such as how to reflect mergers and acquisitions or split out UK-specific reporting from current global reporting commitments.
We’re proud to be leading the way by publishing this data and demonstrating the progress that food and drink manufacturers are making to help consumers make healthier choices. Ensuring we have a stable regulatory environment and consistent reporting metrics will ensure we can go even further.
I would be delighted to meet to discuss how industry can support government in delivering mandatory healthier food sales reporting and the further dietary change that we believe is possible.
Karen Betts OBE
Chief Executive

Too Good To Go is the world’s largest app for surplus […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
From today, over 350 M&S Food stores will offer Too Good To Go Surprise Bags made up of surplus bakery products, giving customers the chance to collect quality food at a reduced price at the end of the day directly from in store bakeries.
Too Good To Go is the world’s largest app for surplus food and the partnership with M&S means customers can now find quality food at a reduced price.
The national launch follows a trial in a select number of stores across the UK and is the latest move in M&S Food’s work to reduce food waste and ensure good food doesn’t go to waste. The Surprise Bags will include bakery treats such as pastries, cookies and bread baked in store.
Each of the Surprise Bags will include three to four bakery products to a minimum retail price of £10.20 for just £3.80. Customers can order their Surprise Bags through the Too Good To Go app and collect them Monday to Saturday, one hour before their local store closes.
The partnership sits alongside M&S’s wider Plan A programme to halve food waste by 2030 and to help edible surplus food find its way to a dinner plate. Just last week, M&S announced that over 130 million meals have been donated from surplus food being redistributed to charities through its partnership with Neighbourly.
In store, M&S repurposes surplus food like bread to make frozen garlic bread and sells bags of bananas that are extra ripe at a reduced price to prevent them from going to waste. M&S uses clear guidance to store food in the right way to prevent waste at home, and store colleagues reduce prices of unsold food before the end of the day to prevent it from going to waste. No food goes to landfill, inedible food that has passed its use by date is sent for anaerobic digestion for renewable energy.
Food waste remains a significant challenge both globally and in the UK. Globally, around 40% of all the food produced around the world is wasted, amounting to as much as 2.5 billion tonnes each year (WWF, 2021). In the UK alone it is estimated that around 10.7 million tonnes of food are wasted every year, with 6.4 million tonnes coming from households (WRAP, 2026).
For Too Good To Go, partnerships with retailers such as M&S provide a practical way to help prevent the food waste challenge, by connecting businesses with customers and giving surplus food another chance to be enjoyed.
Lucinda Langton, head of sustainability at M&S Food, said: “Too Good To Go is a brilliant example of how we’re turning our commitment to reducing food waste into practical action. By giving customers access to surprise bags of surplus bakery products, we can help ensure more of our food is enjoyed. The response from our trial stores has been outstanding, and this partnership is another positive step towards our goal of halving food waste by 2030.”
Chelsea Kerr, managing director at Too Good To Go UK & Ireland, said: “We’re delighted to be partnering with M&S to help make their surplus food available to even more customers across the UK and Ireland. Food waste is a huge challenge, but partnerships like this show how simple it can be for businesses and consumers to take action together. By giving food that might otherwise go unsold another chance to be enjoyed, we’re making it easier for people to save good food while also getting great value. M&S is a much-loved brand across the UK, so we’re excited to be working together to make saving food from going to waste a simple and accessible part of everyday life for even more people.”

items.body:
Office professionals are sparking a major packed lunch revival. Driven by rising costs, workers across the country are swapping store-bought lunches for homemade creations to stretch their budgets further, new supermarket data reveals.
Data from Ocado.com, the UK’s largest dedicated online supermarket, highlights a clear shift in consumer habits. Searches for “lunch bowls” are up 79% year-on-year, alongside strong growth in meal prep staples like microwavable rice (+23% YoY) and ziplock bags (+60% YoY.)
Nearly half of UK professionals (46%) now bring a packed lunch to work more frequently than they did a year ago. The push is largely financial: seven in 10 (69%) say that buying lunch near the office has become too expensive, while 72% say bringing food from home helps them better manage household finances. Nutrition is another core driver, with two-thirds (66%) noting that packed lunches make it easier to eat healthily and track macros or calories.
And social media is accelerating the shift. Content creators like Frankie Parker (161k Instagram followers) regularly share lunchbox ideas as 61% of workers turn online for inspiration. Although traditional sandwiches remain popular (52%), Ocado shoppers are increasingly seeking out more inspired options, with searches soaring for salad bowls (+100%), pasta salad (+24%), and grain bowls (+173%).
Convenient grab-and-go lunchbox snacks are also thriving. With searches for lunchbox snacks spiking 79% and sales of Babybel having risen by 34% on Ocado.
This shift is being driven by younger generations establishing long-term habits, with a quarter of Gen Z and Millennial employees (25%) saying they bring a homemade lunch every day they are in the office. With 64% of this demographic admitting they bring their lunch to work more often than they did last year.
Dan Elton, chief customer officer at Ocado Retail, commented: “Consumers are looking for smart, practical ways to save money, embracing packed lunches as part of their routine to curb everyday on-the-go spending. Our search trends show there is a clear demand for affordable, inspiring options amongst our customers. From grab and go lunchbox staples to nutritious salad bowls and a variety of ingredients that make batch-cook lunch prep easy, Ocado is helping shoppers get more from their lunchboxes whatever their budget or taste.”
With eating out costs continuing to rise, the humble packed lunch has cemented its place as an essential tool for smart household spending across the UK.

items.body:
Matalan, the leading UK fashion and homeware retailer, is marking a major milestone in its transformation as it unveils a new season of product alongside a series of changes to how customers experience the brand.
The progress is now being expressed through Believe It’s Matalan, a new platform that brings Matalan’s evolution to life for customers and is designed to challenge perceptions of the retailer, showcase what it has to offer today and encourage customers to take another look.
The milestone is the culmination of more than a year of customer-led transformation at Matalan. Starting with a deeper understanding of its core customer – what matters to her and her loved ones and what she expects from Matalan – the retailer has evolved its product, stores and digital experience around a clearer proposition of everyday style, quality and value.
The shift is most visible in Matalan’s latest Autumn/Winter 2026 collection. Across womenswear, menswear, kidswear and home, there is a more effortless and modern approach to style, with greater focus on fabric, fit, quality and the design details that elevate the finished product. Particular areas of focus include denim, knitwear, outerwear and jersey, alongside Matalan’s Souluxe sportswear proposition and Taylor & Wright men’s formalwear offer – all while continuing to offer the value customers expect.
Customers are responding to the changes. In the second quarter of this year, Matalan grew both volume and value market share across clothing, footwear and accessories, while also moving from second to first retailer of choice among its core customers, compared with a year ago*. Q1 revenue also grew 2%.
The progress builds on a year of investment across the wider customer experience. Refreshed stores outperformed the wider estate by 12% in the year following their refresh, while online sales grew 10% in FY26.
Matalan has since completed the rollout of its new native app, with 93% of existing app users migrating to the platform in its first month. The app recorded two million sessions over the same period, with average order value 4% higher than on the previous app and 10% higher than on Matalan’s website.
Investment in stores is continuing too, with refreshed layouts, improved navigation and visual merchandising helping customers discover and shop the ranges more easily.
With growing evidence that the changes are resonating with customers, Matalan is building on that momentum with its boldest step yet. Believe It’s Matalan brings the transformation together for customers, putting the Matalan of today front and centre and inviting shoppers to take a fresh look at the brand.
Sarah Welsh, chief product, brand and commercial officer at Matalan, commented: “We’ve had a clear vision for a more modern Matalan for some time, shaped by what our customers have been telling us. This is a really exciting moment because that vision is now coming to life for customers. There’s been a huge amount of work to get here, and you can now see and feel the difference right across the Matalan experience.
“What’s most encouraging is that our customers are responding. Believe It’s Matalan gives us a chance to build on that – to surprise people, challenge some of the old perceptions of Matalan and show them what we have to offer today.”
In the days leading up to the launch of Believe It’s Matalan, Matalan will deliberately keep its name under wraps, putting its new-season product in front of consumers through unbranded teaser activity across outdoor, social, influencer and experiential channels, with only a distinctive red marque hinting at the brand behind it. Activity will include hand-painted murals in London and Liverpool, a red-box experiential pop-up at Westfield London, and an unbranded lookbook around London Fashion Week.
On 12 September, Matalan revealed itself as the brand behind the activity as the full Believe It’s Matalan campaign launched across TV, outdoor, social and other channels – inviting customers to reconsider what they think they know about Matalan.

items.body:
Co-op Wholesale has officially launched a new Nisa Congleton store after the operator switched from his former Morrison’s Daily fascia. It is now open to the public serving a wide selection of award-winning Co-op Brand lines as well as other popular convenience goods.
Located on St John’s Road in the Cheshire town, the new store has benefited from a full fit out of the new Nisa proposition from its previous fascia. Standing at 1,500sqft, the new store is the third Nisa store for business owner Martin Corban.
Corban will operate the store serving the bustling residential area with vital food for now, on the go food and drink solutions, snacks, treats, BWS, fresh, produce and more. The new store gives local shoppers access to a wide range of everyday essentials, fresh food and Co-op brand products, offering them quality, value and convenience. Among the Co-op brand lines available to all Nisa symbols to stock are fresh and chilled, food-to-go, fresh produce, frozen and award-winning premium ranges, under the Irresistible moniker.
Nisa stores uniquely benefit from having access to the Co-op brand, which brings a wealth of benefit to independent retailers’ customers, from recognisable products that fit their lifestyle to solutions for any meal or snacking occasion. Nisa retailers also receive far-reaching support from Co-op Wholesale teams, encompassing operations, supply chain, marketing and more to support the running of their independent business.
Holly Perry, key account manager at Co-op Wholesale, commented: “We’re really pleased to be opening this store with Martin and team as partners. It is in a superb location and is set up to trade well, serve the community and make a brilliant retail business. We wish the team the very best of luck and are certain it will go from strength to strength.”
Martin Corban, owner of Nisa Congleton, commented: “Opening our Nisa store in Congleton marks a really exciting time – we’ve long admired all that comes with being part of the Co-op Wholesale group, including access to the Co-op brand lines, the outstanding expertise and support and the highly recognisable Nisa symbol. The town is undergoing significant housing development meaning quality convenience stores provide a much-needed amenity. We’ve received excellent support from the Co-op Wholesale team and are looking forward to working with them as we grow our business and service this town and beyond.”
Making a difference in the Community (MADL)
A unique point of difference and real draw for Nisa stores is Co-op Wholesale’s charity – Making A Difference Locally (MADL). It supports retail partners through fundraising via Co-op brand products’ sales to support causes local to stores.
Via MADL, £500 has been donated to The Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation – a foundation set up to help children and young adults in need, in and around the local area, as well as charities supporting those affected by road traffic deaths.
Kate Carroll, Social Value Lead said: “The Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation is a charity close to the hearts of the team at Nisa Congleton and was chosen to receive £500 from MADL as part of the launch celebrations. The Foundation was created in memory of Georgia ‘Gee’ Ogden and is a powerful example of turning tragedy into hope for others. The donation will support the Foundation’s work helping children and young adults in need, as well as those affected by road traffic fatalities. We wish the charity every success as it continues to honour Gee’s memory through positive action in local communities.”

items.title: Hugo Boss chair steps down as Mike Ashley's Frasers eyes takeover
items.summary: The chairman of Hugo Boss has stepped down after a year in the role amid pressure from Mike Ashley's Frasers Group.
items.body:
Hugo Boss chair steps down as Mike Ashley's Frasers eyes takeover
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
The chairman of Hugo Boss has stepped down after a year in the role amid pressure from Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group.
The retail giant, owned by the billionaire, has tightened its grip on Hugo Boss in recent months, increasing its shareholding to close to 50 per cent as it eyes a takeover.
The FTSE 100 retailer now plans to appoint a second representative to Hugo Boss’s board after chairman Stephan Sturm ‘decided to step down’ following discussions with Frasers.
It follows months of pressure on Sturm, who was elected chair in May 2025, as Mike Ashley sought to install Michael Murray, Frasers boss and his son-in-law, as Hugo Boss’s chief executive.
Earlier this month, Frasers said it was reviewing whether it supported Sturm as chairman, marking another U-turn for Frasers, which initially opposed his leadership before revising its stance in June.
Closing in: Mike Ashley's Frasers has a near 50% holding in Hugo Boss after takeover attempt
‘Both parties share the view that, as Hugo Boss enters a new chapter in its corporate history, this is an appropriate point in time for an orderly transition in the office of chairman’, Frasers said.
He will serve as chairman until October 15, or until a successor is found.
‘Following the recent changes in the company’s shareholder structure, I believe that this is the right time for an orderly transition in the chairmanship,’ Sturm said.
‘Hugo Boss has an experienced supervisory board, a highly committed managing board and a clear strategic direction. I am convinced that the company is well positioned for future success.’
Frasers has built its holding in Hugo Boss, which it stocks in its Flannels and Frasers shops, since its first investment in 2020, building its stake to around 36 per cent in July.
It offered to pay around £1.7billion for the remaining shares, equivalent to €38 per share, but Hugo Boss rejected the ‘inadequate’ takeover offer.
In August, 17.6 per cent of Hugo Boss investors tendered their shares in support of the bid, bringing Frasers’s stake to nearly 48 per cent.
The proposed takeover of Hugo Boss forms part of Frasers’s push into the luxury market after buying department store chain Harvey Nichols for £40million last month.
Frasers shares rose 0.5 per cent to 796.5p, bringing the year’s gains to 18.88 per cent.

items.body:
Apple’s next Pro-tier iPhone is generating steady interest ahead of an expected autumn launch. Industry reports have circulated for months regarding the device’s chip, camera and pricing, though Apple has confirmed none of the details itself. As with previous cycles, the company is expected to follow its usual September launch window.
What’s expected from the new chip and camera
Reports point to the iPhone 18 Pro carrying Apple’s most advanced chip to date, continuing the company’s pattern of giving the Pro line its newest silicon before other models in the range. Some reports suggest the chip will be built on a more advanced manufacturing process than the current generation, a shift expected to bring improved efficiency alongside stronger performance.
Camera changes are also among the most discussed rumours surrounding the release. Multiple reports point to a variable aperture lens on the main camera, a feature that would allow the device to control depth of field mechanically rather than relying entirely on software processing. That kind of change would mark a meaningful shift for mobile photography, should the reports prove accurate.
Display and battery improvements round out the list of expected changes. Leaks suggest a brighter panel with improved power efficiency, alongside a modest increase in battery capacity over the current model. None of these specifications have been confirmed by Apple, and details are likely to shift before any official announcement.
Pricing expectations and where refurbished fits in
Pricing for the new model is expected to follow a similar structure to previous Pro releases, though analysts have noted that rising chip and component costs could push retail prices higher than the current generation. For consumers weighing up whether to buy new, a refurbished iPhone from a recent generation typically offers most of the performance people rely on day to day, at a lower cost than any new release.
Storage options are also expected to follow the pattern set by recent Pro releases, with a base tier alongside higher-capacity configurations for users with heavier photo and video demands. Colour options typically expand slightly after launch, once initial supply constraints ease.
Interest in refurbished devices tends to increase around a major product launch, as more consumers trade in older phones to help fund an upgrade. That shift generally increases the volume of stock available on the secondary market and tends to bring prices down further than usual.
Back Market is the largest online marketplace dedicated to refurbished electronics, and every device listed through the platform is tested and graded for condition before sale, with a warranty included regardless of the grade selected. That combination of transparency and value has helped shift refurbished technology from a niche alternative into a mainstream purchasing option for retailers and consumers alike.
Whether you wait for the latest hardware or go for a reliable, cheaper option, knowing what each option gives you tends to lead to a better outcome than reacting to launch day pricing. Like any big product cycle, the next few months will likely give us a better idea of both specs and price.

items.title: Southampton brothers turn camping idea into UK’s leading roof tent brand
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Growing up, family holidays meant tents, campervans, campsites and the freedom to spend whole days outdoors. But by the time they were adults, they felt camping had started to mean something very different. For many people, […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Camping gave brothers Ollie and Neill some of their happiest childhood memories and in 2014 it changed their life.
Growing up, family holidays meant tents, campervans, campsites and the freedom to spend whole days outdoors. But by the time they were adults, they felt camping had started to mean something very different.
For many people, it meant ‘roughing it’ , sleeping on cold or wet ground, wrestling with poles and packing huge amounts of equipment into the car. At the other end of the spectrum was a growing image of outdoor adventure as something for hardcore enthusiasts: modified 4x4s, expedition vehicles, specialist kit and remote wilderness.
There seemed to be very little in between. Ollie and Neill saw a market where traditional camping could feel like something you have to endure, while the alternative was an expensive campervan or heavily modified vehicle. Their idea was to use the car people already owned as the starting point for an adventure.
The trip that changed their idea of camping
In 2014, the brothers were travelling through France when they bought a rooftop tent. Suddenly, camping felt different. There was no hunting for the perfect patch of ground, no lengthy tent set-up and no need for a campervan. They could stop somewhere, open the tent above the car, sleep on a proper mattress and move on again the next morning.
And everywhere they went, people wanted to know what it was. The experience convinced them there was an opportunity to take something that was still largely associated with expedition vehicles and make it relevant to ordinary cars and ordinary weekends away.
Two years later, the brothers founded TentBox. The ambition wasn’t to make camping more extreme. It was almost the opposite. They wanted to remove the barriers that made people think camping wasn’t for them.
Childhood experience appears to play a significant role in whether the next generation discovers camping at all.
New research commissioned by TentBox found that parents who count camping among their own fondest childhood memories are more than twice as likely to want to camp with their children (39.8%), compared with 19% of parents overall and 14.6% among those who did not name camping as a favourite childhood memory.
For Ollie and Neill, the finding resonates particularly strongly. Camping formed some of their own happiest childhood memories, but their ambition with TentBox has always been to ensure people don’t need to have grown up camping to feel that the outdoors is for them.
A family should be able to decide on Thursday that they wanted to go away on Friday. Someone without specialist outdoor knowledge should feel just as comfortable using the product as an experienced camper. And adventure shouldn’t require a £50,000 campervan, weeks of preparation or an identity built around being ‘outdoorsy’.
Ten years later
What began with early prototypes developed from Ollie’s garage has grown into the UK’s leading roof-tent brand, with rooftop camping now being used by families, couples, solo travellers and people who may never previously have considered themselves campers.
TentBox is also unapologetic that most of its customers will use its products at campsites, and treats that as something to celebrate. UK campsites are a national treasure: places for spontaneous weekends, easy socialising, family time and a more relaxed kind of adventure. The outdoors doesn’t have to mean remoteness or hardship to be worth the trip.
More than 100,000 TentBoxers are now on the road, with owners swapping campsite recommendations and routes and even organising large community meet-ups known as TentBox Takeovers.
And having helped establish rooftop camping in the UK, the brothers are now taking the idea further.
TentBox is expanding across Europe while continuing to invest in product development from its Southampton headquarters. New products such as TrunkBox are designed around the same question the brothers asked a decade ago: what are the little bits of friction that stop somebody simply deciding to get away? The company also has further product development planned for 2027.
For Ollie and Neill, though, the measure of what they have built is perhaps simpler. It is seeing children running around campsites creating versions of the same memories they had themselves.
Ollie, co-founder of TentBox, said: “When we started TentBox, roof tents in the UK were something you saw on an expedition vehicle, not on a normal car outside a normal house. We thought that was the wrong way round.
“The whole point is that your bed is already there. You arrive, pop it open in minutes, and you’re sleeping up off the cold, wet ground with a proper mattress and usually a pretty great view. No hunting for the perfect patch of grass. You get some of the freedom of a campervan, on the car you already own.
“That changes the psychology of camping. It stops being a logistical exercise and becomes something you decide on a Thursday and do on Friday night. Most of our customers aren’t trying to prove how outdoorsy they are. They just want a good weekend away without the faff.
“Looking at where we are now, the team, the community and the sheer number of trips people have taken with a TentBox is pretty surreal. Ten years on, the ambition hasn’t changed: to help more people get outdoors more often, and to keep designing products that make doing that easier, more comfortable and more fun.”
